dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ): arranged in a firm, solid arrangement, beset by no breach or defect, as though it were a solidly built, well-laid structure. It may also be a transfer by the hamza from حكُم (with ḍamma on the kāf), i.e. "it became wise". It is also said that its meaning is "it was protected from corruption", from their saying أحكمت الدابة, when you put the ḥakama (bit-piece) on the animal to restrain it from mating [Translator's note: so the source; the ḥakama is usually described as restraining the animal from running wild]. Jarīr said:
أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم ... إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا
(O sons of Ḥanīfa, restrain your fools; I fear for you that I may become angry.)
A lengthy discussion of wisdom (ḥikma) in the Qur'an has preceded, and more of it will come as well.

* I'rab:
(الر، كِتابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ): الر — what is said about it has preceded. كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a Book", the clause أحكمت آياته is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, and آياته is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; فصلت is a passive past verb [Translator's note: the source misprints it as «فصت»]; من is a preposition and لدن is an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive; both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) فصلت, or to an omitted naʿt of كتاب — and this is preferable, because it was first described by the firmness of its verses and their detailing, both indicating the loftiness of its rank in itself, and then it was described by this attribute, indicating the loftiness of its standing in terms of its relation [to its Source]. حكيم is in genitive construct to لدن, and خبير is a naʿt of حكيم. (أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنَّنِي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ): أن may be lightened from the heavy [أنّ], its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with لا prohibitive and تعبدوا jussive by لا, the clause being the khabar of the lightened أن. Or أن may be a maṣdar-forming particle that puts in the accusative, with لا negating and the verb after it accusative by أن, and أن with what is in its domain is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) by implying the lām, in the sense of "so that you do not worship". Or it may be explicative (tafsīriyya), because the detailing of the verses carries the sense of speech, as though it were said: "He said: do not worship anyone but Allah," or "He commanded you not to worship anyone but Allah." Perhaps this is easier than the two preceding views, even though the three views are equal in weight. إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إنّ and its noun, with the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) between them; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نذير and بشير; منه is a ḥāl (circumstantial); نذير is the khabar of إنّ and بشير is conjoined to نذير. (وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ): the wāw is a conjunction and أن is conjoined to the first أن, conjoining one reason to another, and it follows the same course in parsing; ربكم is the object of استغفروا, ثم is a conjunction, and توبوا is conjoined to أن استغفروا, so it is a third reason. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «وأن استغفروا» and what follows may be a fresh statement, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, urging people to devote worship exclusively to Allah; this is indicated by his saying: إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير. (يُمَتِّعْكُمْ مَتاعاً حَسَناً إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى): يمتعكم is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request, namely His saying أن استغفروا ربكم; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, متاعا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), حسنا is a naʿt, إلى أجل is attached to يمتعكم, and مسمى is a naʿt of أجل. (وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ): the wāw is a conjunction and يؤت is conjoined to يمتعكم, jussive like it, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is "He", i.e. Allah; كل is a first object, ذي فضل is a muḍāf ilayhi, and فضله is a second object. (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, إن is conditional, تولوا is an imperfect verb whose original form is تتولوا, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), إنّ and its noun, the clause أخاف عليكم is the khabar of إنّ, and the clause فإني أخاف عليكم is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذاب is a mafʿūl bihi, يوم is a muḍāf ilayhi, and كبير is a naʿt of يوم. The Day of Resurrection is described by greatness just as it is described by magnitude and heaviness. (إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): إلى الله is a fronted khabar and مرجعكم a postponed mubtadaʾ; هو is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدير, and قدير is the khabar of هو.

dervis-irab:5-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَثْنُونَ): الثني is bending/turning: you say ثنيته عن كذا, i.e. I turned him away from such-and-such. From it comes الاثنان ("two"), because one of them is turned (joined) onto the other in meaning; from it comes الثناء ("praise"), because of the turning of virtues together in praise; and from it comes الاستثناء ("exception"), because it is turned back upon it by being taken out of it. The original form of يثنون is يثنيون, since it is of the pattern يرمي, its maṣdar being الثني; the ḍamma of the yāʾ was transferred to the nūn before it, and then [the yāʾ] was dropped because two quiescent letters met. So its measure is يفعون [Translator's note: the source prints «يعفون», evidently a misprint for «يفعون»], because the dropped yāʾ is the lām (third radical) of the word. Al-Zamakhsharī said: يثنون عنه: they turn aside from the truth and deviate from it, because one who turns towards a thing faces it with his chest, while one who turns aside from it and deviates turns his chest away from it and folds his flank away from it.
(لِيَسْتَخْفُوا): الاستخفاء is seeking the concealment of a thing; one says استخفى and تخفّى.
(يَسْتَغْشُونَ): they seek a covering. Al-Khansāʾ said:
أرعى النجوم وما كلفت رعيتها ... وتارة أتغشّى فضل اطماري
(I watch the stars, though I was not charged with watching them, and at times I cover myself with the remnant of my worn garments.)
In al-Qāmūs: استغشى ثوبه means he covered himself with it so as not to hear or see.
(الدابة): the living being whose nature is to creep (يدبّ). In usage it has become specific to a kind of animal. In al-Miṣbāḥ: دبّ الصغير يدِبّ, of the pattern ضرب, when a little child walks; and دبّ الجيش دبيبا, the army moved at a gentle pace. Every animal on earth is a دابة.

* I'rab:
(أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُوا مِنْهُ): ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ and its noun, and the clause يثنون صدورهم is its khabar (predicate); the lām is causal, and يستخفوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (أَلا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيابَهُمْ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): ألا reinforces the alerting; حين is an adverb (ẓarf) and what governs it is implied, namely يستخفون. It may also be an adverb of يعلم, i.e. "Indeed, He knows their secret and their open [deeds] when they do such-and-such." The clause يستغشون is in genitive construct to the adverb, ثيابهم is accusative by removal of the preposition, يعلم is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is "He", i.e. Allah, ما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the clause يسرون is the ṣila (relative clause), and ما يعلنون is conjoined to it. (إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): إنّ, its noun and its khabar, and بذات الصدور is attached to (mutaʿalliq) عليم. (وَما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُها): the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), brought to show that He, Exalted is He, encompasses all beings and knows everything that moves. ما is negating, من is redundant (zāʾida), and دابة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) in position, genitive by من in form; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), على الله is a fronted khabar and رزقها a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of دابة. (وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّها وَمُسْتَوْدَعَها): the wāw is a conjunction, يعلم is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "He", مستقرها is the object of يعلم and مستودعها is conjoined to مستقرها. Both are nouns of place, i.e. He knows the places where it settles and its dwellings, and the places where it is deposited, in a loin, a womb or an egg. (كُلٌّ فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): كل is a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it is permissible because of the sense of generality in it, i.e. each one of the creatures. The rules of «كل» will come in the section of Benefits. في كتاب is the khabar and مبين a naʿt (adjective). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, هو is a mubtadaʾ, الذي is the khabar, the clause خلق السموات والأرض is the ṣila, and في ستة أيام is attached to خلق. (وَكانَ عَرْشُهُ عَلَى الْماءِ): كان and its noun, and على الماء is its khabar; in the image there is an embodiment of [His] encompassing. (لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا): the lām is causal and يبلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the genitive-governing causal lām together with what it enters on is attached to خلق. أيكم is a mubtadaʾ, أحسن the khabar, and عملا a tamyīz (specification); the clause is in the position of the accusative as governed by يبلوكم, which is suspended (taʿlīq) from it by the interrogative أي. Al-Zamakhsharī put it well when he said: "If you say: how is it permissible to suspend the verb of testing? I say: because of the sense of knowledge in testing, since it is a path to it, so it is bound up with it — just as you say: 'Look which of them is fairest of face,' and 'Listen which of them is finest of voice,' because looking and listening are among the paths of knowledge." (وَلَئِنْ قُلْتَ إِنَّكُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْمَوْتِ): the wāw is a conjunction and the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa). It cannot be the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), because it has entered on إن, which is for requital, whereas the lām of inception is particular to the noun or what resembles the noun. إن is a particle of condition putting in the jussive, قلت is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); إنّ and its noun, مبعوثون is its khabar, and من بعد الموت is attached to مبعوثون. (لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is dispensed with by the answer to the oath, because when [the oath] comes at the head of the speech it prevails over it — this has preceded. يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, as has preceded. إن is negating, هذا is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, سحر is the khabar and مبين a naʿt. The discussion of the lām and its kinds will come in the section of Benefits. (وَلَئِنْ أَخَّرْنا عَنْهُمُ الْعَذابَ إِلى أُمَّةٍ مَعْدُودَةٍ): لئن is conjoined to what preceded, and the parsing of لئن has preceded; عنهم is attached to أخرنا, العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi, and إلى أمة is attached to أخرنا. What is meant by أمة is a span of time, though originally it is for a group of people. معدودة is a naʿt of أمة. (لَيَقُولُنَّ ما يَحْبِسُهُ): the lām is the answer to the oath, and يقولن is an imperfect verb, nominative because it is separated from the nūn of emphasis by a separator, namely the wāw of the plural, which was dropped because two quiescent letters met. The original form is ليقولوننّ: one of the nūns was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw was dropped because two quiescent letters met, the ḍamma on the lām indicating it. Its verification has preceded, and we have repeated it as a reminder. ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يحبسه is the khabar; the question is for denial, mockery and ridicule, according to their belief. (أَلا يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ): ألا is a particle of interrogation and alerting [Translator's note: so the source; above it called ألا a particle of opening and alerting], and in meaning it enters on ليس. يوم يأتيهم is accusative as an adverb, and it is governed by the khabar of ليس; the noun of ليس is latent (mustatir) in it, referring to the punishment; مصروفا is the khabar of ليس, and عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مصروفا. Reference to the permissibility of placing the khabar of ليس before it will come in the section of Benefits. (وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause حاق is conjoined to the clause ليس, so it is within the domain of ألا; بهم is attached to حاق, ما is the fāʿil of حاق, the clause كانوا is the ṣila, the wāw is the noun of كان, به is attached to يستهزئون, and the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
1- (كُلٌّ) is a noun coined for encompassing the individuals of a plurality, or for covering all the parts of a single thing. It is used only in genitive construct, in wording or by implication. It conveys repetition when the maṣdar-forming adverbial ما enters on it, e.g. كلما أتاك أكرمه ("whenever he comes to you, honour him"). This was dealt with under كلما at His saying «كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا»: it is accusative as an adverb by agreement, what puts it in the accusative is the verb which is the apodosis in meaning, and the clause after it has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of a particle relative. «كل» may be a naʿt of an indefinite or a definite noun, indicating that it is complete, reaching the utmost in what you describe it by, e.g. هو العالم كل العالم ("he is the scholar, the scholar in every sense"). It may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of a definite or indefinite noun, e.g. «فسجد الملائكة كلهم» and أقمنا حولا كاملا كله ("we stayed a full year, all of it"). The word كل is singular and masculine in form, while its meaning is according to what it is put in construct with. If it is put in construct with an indefinite [Translator's note: the source says «مذكر» (masculine); the context and the following contrast with «معرفة» show «منكّر» (indefinite) is intended], its meaning must be observed, and the pronoun after it comes as masculine singular: «وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر»; or feminine singular, e.g. «كل نفس ذائقة الموت»; or dual, as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
وكل رفيقي كل رحل وإن هما ... تعاطى القنا قوما هما اخوان
(Every two companions of every saddle — even if they once traded spear-thrusts as enemies — are brothers.)
Ibn Hishām has a forced and confused parsing of this verse; we content ourselves with pointing to it so that whoever wishes may refer to it in Mughnī al-Labīb.
Or masculine plural, as in the saying of Labīd:
وكل أناس سوف تدخل بينهم ... دويهية تصفر منها الأنامل
(Every people — a small calamity will enter among them from which the fingertips turn pale.)
Or feminine plural, as in the saying of another: وكل مصيبات الزمان وجدتها ... سوى فرقة الأحباب هينة الخطب
(All the calamities of time I have found, except separation from loved ones, light in their burden.)
If it is put in construct with a definite noun, it is permissible to observe its form or to observe its meaning, so one says:
كل القوم حضر and كل القوم حضروا ("all the people came"). If it is cut off from construct in wording, it is said that it is permissible to observe the form or the meaning, e.g. كل حضر and كل حضروا; and it is said that if what is implied is an indefinite singular, the singular is obligatory, and if it is a definite plural, the plural is obligatory. The tanwīn in [كل] cut off from construct in wording is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi; the implied form in the first example is كل أحد and in the second كلهم. If كل occurs after a negation, [the negation applies to the whole, and the affirmation is] established for some of the individuals, e.g. ما جاء كل القوم ("not all the people came"); and if the negation occurs after it, [the negation] is established for every individual, e.g. كلهم لم يقوموا ("none of them stood"). [Translator's note: the source's wording «وإن وقعت كل بعد النفي ثابتا لبعض الأفراد» is elliptical; the bracketed words give the evident sense.] Al does not enter on it unless it is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi, or its word itself is intended, as one says الكل for encompassing the individuals.
2- The lām: the lām is of three kinds: governing the genitive, governing the jussive, and non-governing.

Its kinds:
a- The genitive lām: it is with kasra with an overt noun, e.g. لزيد, except with the one called for help (al-mustaghāth) directly after «يا», where it has fatḥa, e.g. يا لله; and it has fatḥa with a pronoun, except with the yāʾ, where it has kasra, e.g. لك and لي.
The genitive lām is of two kinds:
a- The lām entering on the noun. It has many meanings mentioned in the lengthy books of grammar; the best known are: specification, e.g. «الجنة للمؤمن»; entitlement, e.g. «العزة لله»; ownership, e.g. «لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض»; conveying, e.g. «قلت له»; making transitive, e.g. «ما أشد حب زيد لعمرو»; oath, e.g. «لله لأفعلن هذا», i.e. "by Allah"; and outcome (ṣayrūra), e.g. «ولد الإنسان لحياة أبدية». It also comes in the sense of إلى, على, عند, في and بعد. It may be redundant (zāʾida), e.g. ضربت لزيد.
b- As for the lām entering on the verb, the verb after it is accusative by an implied maṣdar-forming أن, and أن with what is in its domain is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the lām. This is either for cause, e.g. «جئتك لتعلمني»; or for outcome, e.g. «فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا»; or for emphasising negation, which is preceded by a negated كون and is called the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), e.g. ما كان زيد ليكذب.
2- The jussive lām: it is the lām of command, also called the lām of request. It has kasra, e.g. «لينفق ذو سعة من سعته», and it may have fatḥa. Making it quiescent after the fāʾ and the wāw is more frequent than voweling it, e.g. «فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي», and it may be made quiescent after ثم, e.g. «ثم ليقض».
3- The non-governing [lām]: it always has fatḥa, and it is:
a- The lām of inception, e.g. «لزيد قائم» and «إن زيدا لقائم»; after إنّ it is called the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
b- The lām of answer after لو, لولا and the oath, e.g. «لو عدتم لعدنا», «لولا زيد لهلكنا» and «والله لزيد كريم».
c- The redundant lām, as in the saying «أراك لشاتمي».
d- The lām of distance attached to demonstratives; its origin is sukūn, as in تلك, and it was given kasra in ذلك only because two quiescent letters met.
3- ليس, its noun and its khabar:
Among the sisters of كان, ليس is distinguished by certain matters:
1- ليس is a verb that does not inflect in any way, because it was put in the place of a particle, in that its meaning is not understood except together with what it relates to.
2- According to the majority of grammarians its khabar may not be placed before it. Some of the early Basrans, al-Farrāʾ, and among the later ones Ibn Burhān and al-Zamakhsharī permitted it, on the basis of His saying, Exalted is He: «ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم». The argument from it runs: يوم يأتيهم is governed by مصروفا and has been placed before ليس, and fronting the governed word is valid only where fronting its governor is valid; so were it not permissible to front the khabar, مصروفا, before ليس, it would not be permissible to front what it governs before it. The reply was that the governed word is an adverb, and with it there is latitude that there is not with other words; or that يوم is governed by an omitted verb, its implied form being "they will know the day it comes to them", and ليس مصروفا is an emphasising ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, or resumptive. Abū Ḥayyān said: "I have searched through a number of the dīwāns of the Arabs and have not come across the khabar of ليس placed before it, nor what it governs, except what the outward sense of the verse indicates."
4- A comment by Ibn Hishām on al-Zamakhsharī, in his note on His saying, Exalted is He:
«ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا». [He said that] al-Zamakhsharī's statement was confused; then he cited what we have quoted from him, and said: "I have not come across the suspension of visual looking and of listening except from him."
Al-Raḍī mentioned that the verbs of the senses are suspended because they are paths to knowledge. ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Baghdādī said in his commentary on [al-Raḍī's] shawāhid on al-Kāfiya: al-Raḍī's book was not brought to Cairo until after the death of Ibn Hishām; that is why he said "I have not come across…" etc.

dervis-irab:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً): what is said about لئن has preceded. أذقنا is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), نا is the fāʿil (agent), الإنسان is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), منّا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة and was placed before it, and رحمة is a second object.
(ثُمَّ نَزَعْناها مِنْهُ إِنَّهُ لَيَؤُسٌ كَفُورٌ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نزعناها is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزعناها; إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), يئوس is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ and كفور is a second khabar of إنّ.
(وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْناهُ نَعْماءَ بَعْدَ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ): the parsing of its like has preceded. بعد is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted naʿt of نعماء; ضراء is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), a diptote because it ends in the extended alif of the feminine; and the clause مسته is a naʿt. (لَيَقُولَنَّ ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئاتُ عَنِّي): the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the clause ذهب السيئات is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl), and عني is attached to ذهب. (إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ): إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām; فرح is a first khabar and فخور a second khabar of إنّ. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ): إلا is a particle of exception and الذين is excepted from الإنسان, because the lām in it is generic, so the exception is connected; it may also be a disconnected exception, since what is meant is a particular person. In either case it is in the position of the accusative. The clause صبروا is the ṣila (relative clause), and عملوا الصالحات is conjoined. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لهم is a fronted khabar and مغفرة a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

* Rhetoric:
1- In "making taste" there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), because it is originally taking a thing in the mouth to perceive food, and it was then borrowed for pleasure, likening it to what is tasted and then quickly vanishes, as flavours vanish.
2- Between النعماء and الضراء there is antithesis (ṭibāq). All of these topics have been discussed before.

* Benefits:
السراء, النعماء and الضراء: it is said that they are maṣdars (verbal nouns) meaning المسرة (gladness), النعمة (favour) and المضرة (harm). The correct view is that they are nouns of maṣdars (asmāʾ al-maṣādir), not the maṣdars themselves: السراء is ease, النعماء is favour, and الضراء is hardship; they are names for these meanings. If we say they are maṣdars, they denote the act itself, which is the meaning; and if they are names for them, they denote what brings about these meanings.

dervis-irab:12-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضائِقٌ): active participle of ضاق. It is more fitting in the verse than ضيّق for two reasons: first, that it is incidental and not by way of permanence; second, that it is more similar to تارك.

* I'rab:
(فَلَعَلَّكَ تارِكٌ بَعْضَ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ وَضائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ): the fāʿ is resumptive. لعل is in its normal sense of hope, relative to the one addressed; it is also said to be for the interrogative of denial, like his saying ﷺ: "Perhaps we have hurried you." What is said about لعل will come in the section of Benefits. The kāf is its noun and تارك is its khabar (predicate); بعض is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of تارك; ما is a relative noun in genitive construct to بعض, the clause يوحى is the ṣila (relative clause), and إليك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوحى or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ضائق is conjoined to تارك, به is attached to ضائق, and صدرك is the fāʿil (agent) of ضائق. Or ضائق may be a fronted khabar and صدرك a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a second khabar of لعلّك; it would then have been predicated with two khabars, one a single word and the second a clause conjoined to a single word because it has its meaning.
(أَنْ يَقُولُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ جاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ): أن with what is in its domain is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear of their saying". Some parsed it as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in His saying وضائق به صدرك, and that is not far-fetched. لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍ), أنزل is a passive past verb, عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it, and كنز is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أو is a conjunction, جاء is a past verb, معه is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to جاء, and ملك is the fāʿil. (إِنَّما أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ): إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنت is a mubtadaʾ and نذير its khabar; الله is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is attached to وكيل, and وكيل is the khabar of الله. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): أم is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) in the sense of بل; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the clause افتراه is the speech reported by "say". It is an affirmation in the form of a question, the implied form being "Nay, do they say: he invented it?"
(قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ مُفْتَرَياتٍ): the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ, ائتوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, بعشر is attached to it, سور is a muḍāf ilayhi, and مثله is a naʿt (adjective). Even though مثل is singular in form, the dual, the plural and the feminine are described by it, as in His saying, Exalted is He, «أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا»; agreement is also permissible — He, Exalted is He, said: «وحور عين كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون». [Translator's note: the source does not parse مفتريات; it is a further naʿt of سور.] (وَادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): ادعوا is conjoined to فأتوا, the wāw is the fāʿil, من is a mafʿūl bihi, the clause استطعتم is the ṣila, and من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. إن is conditional, كنتم is كان and its noun, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); صادقين is the khabar of كنتم, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring and call". (فَإِلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ): the fāʿ is a conjunction, إن is conditional, لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and the jussive, and يستجيبوا is jussive by لم; it is the protasis, and the wāw is the fāʿil, the pronoun referring to "those you are able [to call]". لكم is attached to يستجيبوا; the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), اعلموا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and أنما is the restraining and restrained; together with what it enters on it takes the place of the two objects of اعلموا. أنزل is a passive past verb, and بعلم الله is a ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with the knowledge of Allah", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa). (وَأَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ):
وأن: the wāw is a conjunction and أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ]; it is conjoined to the أن before it. لا إله إلا هو has been parsed fully before. The fāʿ is a conjunction, هل is an interrogative particle, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and مسلمون is the khabar.

* Benefits:
(لعل) is for expectation; some expressed it as hope (tarajjī) in something loved, e.g. لعل الحبيب قادم ("perhaps the beloved is coming") and His saying, Exalted is He, «لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا»; and apprehension (ishfāq) in something disliked, e.g. «فلعلك باخع نفسك», i.e. "killing yourself", the meaning being "I fear for you that you will kill yourself out of grief at what you missed of your people's embracing Islam". So expecting something loved is called hope, and expecting something disliked is called apprehension. Al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī said: لعل also comes for cause, e.g. «افرغ من عملك لعلنا نتغدى» ("finish your work so that we may have lunch"), and from it is His saying, Exalted is He, «لعله يتذكر», i.e. "so that he may remember". The Kufans said لعل comes for interrogation. He said in al-Mughnī: for this reason the verb is suspended by it, e.g. «لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا» and His saying, Exalted is He, «وما يدريك لعله يزكى». Some Arabs put [the following noun] in the genitive with it, and they cite as evidence for that the saying:
فقلت ادع أخرى وارفع الصوت جهرة ... لعل أبي المغوار منك قريب
(So I said: call once more and raise your voice aloud; perhaps Abū al-Mighwār is near you.)
Once you know what the grammarians have established, which of the meanings of لعل applies to the verse we are dealing with? If it is for expectation, then the expectation of abandoning the conveying [of the message] does not befit the station of prophethood. They answered this objection by saying that we do not concede that لعل is here in its normal sense of hope; rather, it is here for making [something] seem remote, for it is used for that too. Another answer is that it is here for the interrogative of denial, as has preceded. [And] the meaning [is]: you have reached the utmost effort in conveying to them, [so do] they expect from you that you abandon conveying some of it? — and this is very fine. [Translator's note: the final sentence is elliptical in the source («والمعنى انك بلغ الجهد في تبليغهم انهم يتوقعون منك ترك التبليغ لبعضه»); the bracketed words supply the evident sense.]

dervis-irab:15-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَزِينَتَها): الزينة is enhancing a thing by something else, such as clothing, ornament or appearance. One says زانه يزينه زينة and زيّنه يزيّنه تزيينا.
(نُوَفِّ): التوفية is rendering what is due in full.
(يُبْخَسُونَ): البخس is diminishing what is due, and every wrongdoer is باخس. In the proverb: «تحسبها حمقاء وهي باخس» ("you think her a fool, yet she is a cheat").

* I'rab:
(مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وَزِينَتَها نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ فِيها وَهُمْ فِيها لا يُبْخَسُونَ): من is a conditional noun putting in the jussive, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the noun of كان is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من, and the clause يريد الحياة الدنيا is the khabar (predicate) of كان; كان is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive in position; زينتها is conjoined to الحياة; نوفّ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نوفّ, أعمالهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and فيها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). وهم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), هم is a mubtadaʾ, فيها is attached to يبخسون, and the clause لا يبخسون is the khabar of هم. Al-Farrāʾ said:
كان here is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being من يرد الحياة الدنيا. This is a fine and elegant view [Translator's note: the source has «ضريف», a misspelling of «ظريف»], were it not that it is not regular, and it is not permissible to interpret the Qur'an by it. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الذين its khabar; the clause ليس is the ṣila (relative clause); لهم is the fronted khabar of ليس, في الآخرة is a ḥāl, إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and النار is the postponed noun of ليس. (وَحَبِطَ ما صَنَعُوا فِيها وَباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, حبط is a past verb, ما is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause صنعوا is the ṣila. ما may also be maṣdar-forming, so that together with what it enters on it is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), the fāʿil of حبط. فيها is attached to صنعوا or to حبط. وباطل: the wāw is a conjunction, باطل is a fronted khabar and ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; ما may also be maṣdar-forming, so that together with what it enters on it is in the sense of a maṣdar, a postponed mubtadaʾ. كانوا is كان and its noun, and the clause يعملون is its khabar.

dervis-irab:17-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البينة): the decisive proof that separates truth from falsehood.
(مِرْيَةٍ): المرية, with kasra and with ḍamma, is doubt. It thus has two dialectal forms, the better known being the kasra, which is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, while the ḍamma is the dialect of Banū Asad.
(لا جَرَمَ): al-Suyūṭī said in al-Itqān: "It occurs in the Qur'an in five places, followed by أنّ and its noun, and no verb comes after it. There is disagreement about it: it is said that لا negates what preceded, and it is said that it is redundant (zāʾida)."
Moreover, there is a long disagreement among the grammarians about this expression, and that disagreement may be summarised as follows:
First: the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, namely that it is compounded of the negating لا and جرم, the two being made indeclinable (mabnī) in their compounding like the compounding of خمسة عشر, and their meaning becoming the meaning of a verb, namely حقّ ("it is true/due"). On this view what follows them is nominative as the fāʿil (agent); so His saying, Exalted is He, «لا جرم أن لهم النار» means: it is true and established that the Fire is theirs, or that it is settled for them.
Second: that لا جرم is like لا رجل, in that لا is the lā of generic negation and جرم is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; لا with its noun is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows them is the khabar (predicate) of لا, and its meaning becomes "inevitably" and "there is no escaping" that they will be in the Hereafter, i.e. in their loss. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ.
Third: that لا negates previous speech which the disbelievers uttered, and Allah refuted that for them by saying لا, just as it occurs before the oath in His saying «لا أقسم». Then after it He brought a verbal clause, namely جرم أن لهم كذا; جرم is a past verb meaning "earned", its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to their deeds as indicated by the context, and أنّ with what is in its domain is in the position of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because جرم is transitive when it means "earned". On this view one pauses on لا and then begins with جرم, unlike what preceded.
Fourth: that its meaning is "no limit and no preventing", جرم having the sense of cutting off — you say جرمت, i.e. I cut off. So جرم is the noun of لا, indeclinable with it on the fatḥa, as we have stated [Translator's note: the source prints «نقدم», read «تقدم»], and its khabar is أنّ with what is in its domain, on the omission of the preposition, i.e. "there is no preventing their loss".
There are several dialectal forms of this expression: لا جِرم with kasra on the jīm, لا جُرم with ḍamma, لا جَرَ with the mīm dropped, لا ذا جرم, لا ذو جرم and others. In any case, this expression is used for a matter that is decided upon and not doubted.

* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr), the fāʿ is resumptive, and من is a relative, a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "like someone else" or "like one who is not so". The answer to the question is also omitted, its implied form being "they are not equal". كان is a defective past verb, its noun is latent, referring to من, على بينة is its khabar, and من ربه is a naʿt (adjective) of بينة. (وَيَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنْهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and يتلوه شاهد is an imperfect verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; منه is a naʿt of شاهد. (وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إِماماً وَرَحْمَةً): the wāw is again a conjunction, and من قبله is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كتاب موسى, which is conjoined to شاهد as a conjoining of single words. This is how most of the commentators parsed it. I hold that the truth lies with al-Bayḍāwī, who parsed من قبله as a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar, with كتاب موسى a postponed mubtadaʾ; for in this parsing there is freedom from the convolution arising from separating the conjunction from what is conjoined [Translator's note: so the source; it is the conjoined element (al-maʿṭūf) that is separated from the conjunction]. إماما is a ḥāl from كتاب موسى and رحمة is conjoined to إماما. (أُولئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يؤمنون به is the khabar. (وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ الْأَحْزابِ فَالنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, يكفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), به is attached to يكفر, and من الأحزاب is a ḥāl; the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), النار is a mubtadaʾ and موعده the khabar, and the nominal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). In making the Fire a "promised meeting-place" there is an intimation that it holds kinds of torment beyond what description can encompass. Ḥassān clung to the fringes of this expression and said:
أوردتموها حياض الموت ضاحية ... فالنار موعدها والموت لا قيها
(You led them down to the pools of death in open daylight; so the Fire is their appointed place and death is what meets them.)
(فَلا تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْهُ): the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ, لا is prohibitive, and تك is an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; the noun of تك is latent, implied as "you"; في مرية is the khabar and منه is a naʿt of مرية. (إِنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ):
إنّ and its noun, الحق is its khabar, and من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), لكنّ and its noun, الناس is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar of لكنّ. (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to mention their fourteen attributes, the first of which is the forging of lies and the last their being in the Hereafter the greatest losers. من is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, and the question here means negation, i.e. "no one is more unjust". ممن is attached to أظلم, the clause افترى is the ṣila (relative clause), على الله is attached to افترى, and كذبا is a mafʿūl bihi. (أُولئِكَ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلى رَبِّهِمْ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعرضون is its khabar; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and على ربهم is attached to يعرضون.
(وَيَقُولُ الْأَشْهادُ هؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى رَبِّهِمْ أَلا لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ): يقول is conjoined to يعرضون and الأشهاد is the fāʿil; هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ and الذين its khabar, and the clause كذبوا على ربهم is the ṣila of the relative noun; ألا is a particle of alerting, لعنة الله is a mubtadaʾ and على الظالمين the khabar. (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً): الذين is a badal (substitute) from الظالمين, the clause يصدون is the ṣila, عن سبيل الله is attached to يصدون, and يبغونها is conjoined to يصدون — it is a verb, its fāʿil and its object; عوجا is a ḥāl, i.e. crooked. (وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ كافِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ, بالآخرة is attached to كافرون, the second هم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first هم, and كافرون is the khabar of the first «هم». (أُولئِكَ لَمْ يَكُونُوا مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, the clause لم يكونوا is the khabar, معجزين is the khabar of يكونوا, and في الأرض is a ḥāl, i.e. they do not escape His grasp in any case. (وَما كانَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negating, كان is a defective past verb, لهم is the fronted khabar of كان, من دون الله is a ḥāl, من is a redundant preposition, and أولياء is the noun of كان in position. (يُضاعَفُ لَهُمُ الْعَذابُ ما كانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ وَما كانُوا يُبْصِرُونَ): يضاعف is a passive imperfect verb, لهم is attached to it, العذاب is the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. ما is negating, كانوا is كان and its noun, the clause يستطيعون السمع is the khabar of كان, and السمع is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع gives the reason for the doubling of the punishment, and the clause وما كانوا يبصرون is conjoined to ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع. The meaning of this speech will come in the section of Rhetoric. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ):
أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and الذين the khabar; the clause خسروا أنفسهم is the ṣila; ضل عنهم is conjoined; ما is the fāʿil of ضل, and the clause كانوا يفترون is the ṣila. (لا جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ): لا is negating and جرم is a past verb; أنهم: أنّ with what is in its domain is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of جرم. We have followed the view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl — see the section of Vocabulary. في الآخرة is a ḥāl; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ, and الأخسرون is the khabar of أنّ, or the khabar of هم, with the clause being the khabar of أنّ. Parallels of the pronoun of separation have preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون» there is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī), because it is a likening of a compound to a compound: He likened them, in their extreme feigned deafness to hearing the truth and their ears' aversion to it, to one who is unable to hear. This is on a number of views:
First: the punishment is doubled for them because they were able to hear yet did not hear, and because they were able to see yet did not see, out of obstinacy and persistence on their part in error and in turning away from the truth. This requires that ما be maṣdar-forming and that the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) be accusative by removal of the preposition, namely the bāʾ, after the manner of the poet's saying:
نغالي اللحم للأضياف نيا ... وتبذله إذا نضج القدور
(We pay a high price for the meat for our guests while it is raw, and give it away freely when the pots are cooked.) He meant نغالي باللحم. Al-Farrāʾ took this view.
Second: that because they found hearing the verses of Allah burdensome and disliked remembering and understanding them, they were treated like one who cannot hear; and their sight did not benefit them, given their turning away from the warnings of the verses, so it was as though they did not see. Of the same kind is the saying of al-Aʿshā at the opening of his muʿallaqa:
ودّع هريرة إنّ الرّكب مرتحل ... وهل تطيق وداعا أيّها الرّجل
(Bid farewell to Hurayra, for the riders are departing — but can you bear a farewell, O man?)
It is well known that al-Aʿshā was able to bid farewell; he denied himself the ability only in the sense of aversion and finding it burdensome.
Third: that ما here is adverbial and maṣdar-forming, after the manner of سأذكرك ما حييت ("I will remember you as long as I live"); the meaning is that they are punished as long as they are alive.

dervis-irab:23-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَخْبَتُوا): they became calm and at ease and turned [to Him] in repentance. الإخبات is tranquillity; its origin is levelness, from الخبت, which is low-lying, level, wide ground; so it is as though الإخبات were continuous humility with evenness in it. It is made transitive with إلى and with the lām: if you say أخبت فلان إلى كذا, its meaning is "he was at ease with it", and if you say أخبت له, its meaning is "he humbled himself and submitted to him". The khāʾ and the bāʾ as the first and second radicals of a word have a strange peculiarity, in that the word indicates the meaning of covering, veiling and concealment, or what is close to that, or connected to it by some link. Thus their saying خبأ الشيء: he veiled it and hid it; له خبيئة: he has a hidden store he has put away for a day of need; and among their proverbs: «لا مخبأ لعطر بعد عروس» ("no hiding perfume after the bride"); "and Allah brings forth الخبء (what is hidden)"; خبّأت الجارية, جارية مخبّأة and نساء مخبّآت (a secluded girl, secluded women) [Translator's note: the source prints «خبّات»]. خبّ الرجل: the man went down into a depression in the ground so that his halting-place would be unknown. خبّ الفرس خبّا وخبيبا: the horse alternated in its running between its forelegs and its hind legs. الخِبّ, with kasra on the khāʾ, is deceit, which is the concealment of cunning; and in the ḥadīth of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: "No one speaks Persian but he becomes cunning (خبّ), and no one becomes cunning but his manliness departs." خبث فلان is the opposite of طاب; the wicked one (الخبيث) conceals the opposite of what he shows. خبر الشيء: he knew it by experience, i.e. he penetrated to its inner parts and made them clear. Baking bread (خبز الخبز) is well known, and its placing [in the oven] amounts to hiding it there. اختبس الشيء: he took it and seized it as booty. خبش الأشياء: he gathered things from here and there. خبص الشيء بالشيء: he mixed one thing with the other. خبط البعير بيده الأرض: the camel struck the ground with its foreleg; بات يختبط الظلماء: he spent the night stumbling through the darkness; and "he is خابط عشوة" is said of the ignorant man. خبع في المكان: he entered into the place; and one says جارية خبعة طلعة, i.e. a girl who sometimes hides herself and sometimes shows herself.
خبله: he corrupted it, or corrupted his mind, and corruption of the mind is its loss. [The poet] said:
أرى المال أفياء الظلال فتارة ... يؤوب وأخرى يخبل المال خابله
(I see wealth as shifting shadows: at one time it returns, and at another its destroyer destroys it.)
خبن الثوب: he folded the garment and stitched it. خبن الشاعر: the poet used khabn in his poetry, which is the dropping of the second letter of a foot when it is quiescent. خبت النار: the fire died down and became still. استخبأ الخباء: he entered the tent. Had we wished to expand on quotation from this root, we would have shown you wonder upon wonder; but enough of the necklace for you is what encircles the neck.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَأَخْبَتُوا إِلى رَبِّهِمْ): إنّ and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), the clause وعملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا, and likewise the clause وأخبتوا إلى ربهم. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أصحاب الجنة the khabar (predicate); هم is a mubtadaʾ, فيها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدون, and خالدون is the khabar of هم. The clause أولئك أصحاب الجنة is the khabar of إنّ, and the clause هم فيها خالدون is a second khabar of إنّ. (مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَالْأَعْمى وَالْأَصَمِّ وَالْبَصِيرِ وَالسَّمِيعِ): مثل is a mubtadaʾ, الفريقين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and كالأعمى is the khabar; or the kāf is a noun meaning مثل, the khabar, and what follows is conjoined to it. (هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلًا أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): هل is interrogative, meaning negation; يستويان is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; مثلا is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), the original being هل يستوي مثلهم. أفلا تذكرون: the question is for denial and rebuke.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «مثل الفريقين etc.» there is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī), i.e. the likeness of the party of the Muslims is as the seeing and the hearing, and the likeness of the party of the disbelievers is as the blind and the deaf. The verse surpasses all examples of the representational simile, such as the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
كأن قلوب الطير رطبا ويابسا ... لدى وكرها العناب والحشف البالي
(As though the hearts of birds, fresh and dried, by its nest were jujube berries and old withered dates.) And the saying of Bashshār:
كأن مثار النقع فوق رءوسنا ... وأسيافنا، ليل تهاوى كواكبه
(As though the dust raised above our heads, and our swords, were a night whose stars are falling.)
In the first verse there is a likening of the fresh hearts of birds to jujubes and a likening of the dried hearts of birds to old withered dates; and in the second verse a likening of the dark dust and the swords flashing in it to the night in which meteors and stars plunge down.
As for the verse, it goes further by likening two things to four, as is clear: it likens each of the disbeliever and the believer with two likenings.
Moreover, had the verse come in the manner of antithesis (ṭibāq), contrary to its arrangement, by saying:
كالأعمى والبصير والأصم والسميع, the meaning would have been spoiled, even though antithesis would have been achieved in the wording. For He, Glorified is He, divided what is likened-to into two divisions like what is likened, because it is two divisions, the afflicted and the sound, and He set them in opposition so that the question between them would be sound, with the aim of rebuke.

dervis-irab:25-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَراذِلُنا): our lowest ones. There are two views about it. The first is that it is a plural of a plural: it is the plural of أرذُل (with ḍamma on the dhāl), the plural of رذْل (with sukūn), like كلب, أكلب and أكالب. The second is that it is the plural of a singular, namely أرذل, like أكبر and أكابر, أبطح and أباطح, أبرق and أبارق; الأرذل is that which is shunned for its poor quality. Al-Zamakhsharī chose the second view, and the author of al-Qāmūs preferred it.
(بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ): the outward [first] opinion. It may be pronounced with a hamza, giving بادئ الرأي. Whoever does not use the hamza meant: "you, in what appears of opinion"; and whoever uses the hamza meant:
"you, at the first of opinion and its beginning". Abū ʿAlī has a fine discussion of this expression, which we quote in full for its benefit:
"The meaning for whoever said بادي الرأي without hamza, making it from بدا in the sense of 'appeared', is: none followed you but the lowest, in what appeared to them of opinion, without following it up with examination of it and deliberation. These two words are close in meaning, because [a root whose] lām (third radical) is a hamza means the beginning of a thing and its first, and when the lām is a wāw the meaning is appearing; and the beginning of a thing is an appearing, so each of them is used in place of the other. It is permissible for the active participle to be an adverb (ẓarf), just as it is permissible for faʿīl, e.g. قريب and مليء, because fāʿil and faʿīl alternate in meaning, e.g. عالم and عليم, شاهد and شهيد. What made that good is its being in genitive construct with الرأي. They have also treated the maṣdar (verbal noun) in this way in being put in construct with it, in their saying اما جهد رأيي فإني منطلق ('as for the utmost of my opinion, I am departing'), and this can only be an adverb" — to the end of this delightful discussion. More will come in the I'rab.
(الرَّأْيِ): maṣdar of رأى رأيا; its plural is آراء. Opinion is reflecting on the beginnings of matters, considering their consequences, and knowing what they lead to of error and correctness. The "people of opinion" (aṣḥāb al-raʾy) according to the jurists are the people of analogy (qiyās) and interpretation. The poets have agreed in praising opinion. Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī said:
ولا أرضى الفتى ما لم يكمل ... برأي الكهل أقدام الغلام
(I am not satisfied with a young man unless he completes the boldness of youth with the judgement of a mature man.)
And Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said:
الرأي قبل شجاعة الشجعان ... هو أول وهي المحل الثاني
فإذا هما اجتمعا لنفس حرة ... بلغت من العلياء كل مكان
(Judgement comes before the courage of the brave: it is first and courage holds second place; and when the two come together in a free soul, it reaches every summit of eminence.)

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ): a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause, brought to begin mentioning a number of stories as consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, as a lesson from them, and as a model in what their protagonists encountered. This sūra contains seven stories. The lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa), قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), نوحا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. إني is with kasra on the hamza on the intention of [an implied verb of] saying, which is often implied, needing no evidence. إنّ and its noun, لكم is attached to نذير, نذير is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ and مبين is its naʿt (adjective).
(أَنْ لا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ): أن is explicative (mufassira), لا is prohibitive, تعبدوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi; إنّ and its noun, the clause أخاف is its khabar, عليكم is attached to أخاف, عذاب يوم is the object of أخاف, and أليم is a naʿt of يوم. (فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ):
the fāʿ is a conjunction, قال الملأ is a verb and its fāʿil, الذين is a naʿt of الملأ, the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), and من قومه is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَراذِلُنا بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ): the clause is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl). ما is negating, and نراك is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction. The seeing may be mental or visual, so بشرا is a second object on the first view and a ḥāl on the second; مثلنا is a naʿt. وما نراك is conjoined to the first ما نراك, and it too may be mental or visual, so the clause اتبعك is either a second object or a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction, الذين is the fāʿil of اتبعك, هم أراذلنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is the ṣila. بادي الرأي is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "at the first of opinion", and what governs it is اتبعك; what is said about it has preceded at length. It is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of Nūḥ in اتبعك, i.e. "while you are of exposed opinion, with no sound judgement". (وَما نَرى لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا مِنْ فَضْلٍ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كاذِبِينَ): وما نرى is conjoined to what preceded, لكم is attached to نرى, علينا is attached to فضل, من is a redundant preposition, and فضل is genitive in form, a mafʿūl bihi accusative in position; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, نظنكم is conjoined to ما نرى, the kāf is a first object and كاذبين a second object. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَآتانِي رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to address them gently, and among it is calling them "[my] people" [Translator's note: the source's «ومنا صفتهم» appears corrupt; this rendering follows the evident intent]. يا قوم is the one addressed (munādā), in genitive construct to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker. أرأيتم has been discussed in detail before; رأيتم is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. "tell me". Here [أرأيتم] requires البينة as a mafʿūl bihi, and كنت requires البينة in the genitive with على; so the second was given governance and [a pronoun] was implied in the first. The implied form is: "Have you considered the clear proof from my Lord, if I am upon it — shall we compel you to it?" So the first object was omitted, the interrogative clause is the second object, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because it is indicated. إن is conditional, كنت is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, على بينة is the khabar of كنت, and من ربي is a naʿt. The meaning of على here is elevation, because the possessor of a clear proof is elevated above others; it is also said to be for accompaniment in the sense of مع, and that is not far-fetched. وآتاني: the wāw is a conjunction, and آتاني is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; رحمة is a second object and من عنده is a naʿt of رحمة. (فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوها وَأَنْتُمْ لَها كارِهُونَ): the fāʿ is a conjunction, عميت is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as "it"; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عميت. The explanation of the reality of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. أنلزمكموها: the hamza is interrogative, i.e. "shall we force you to it?" In this verb there are three pronouns: the first is latent, implied as "we", and it is the fāʿil; the second is the pronoun of the one addressed, i.e. the kāf, and it is the first object; the third is the pronoun of the absent, i.e. the hāʾ, and it is the second object. The mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, and the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma on the mīm and is not a pronoun. The order among them has been observed, because the speaker is the most specific to the verb, then the pronoun of the one addressed, then the pronoun of the absent. وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, لها is attached to كارهون, and كارهون is the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. What is said about the clause أنلزمكموها has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In attributing blindness to the clear proof there is a rational metonymic attribution (majāz ʿaqlī), treating it as a rational being. Its reality is that the argument and the clear proof, which were made a source of insight and enabling sight, were made blind, because the blind man is not guided and does not guide others. So the clear proof was made blind to you and did not guide you, just as if the scout of a people, who leads them through dark wildernesses and branching deserts, were struck blind to them, so that they remained bewildered, stumbling about and seeking deliverance from their bewilderment. Some of them made it a case of inversion (qalb), i.e. that it was they who were blinded, so that it is of the type "I put the ring into my finger" and "I put the cap into my head" [i.e. instead of "my finger into the ring"]. The poet said: ترى الشوك فيها مدخلا ظل رأسه ... وسائره باد إلى الشمس أجمع
(You see the [ostrich] in it with the shade [of the tree] made to enter its head [i.e. its head put into the shade], while the rest of it is wholly exposed to the sun.) [Translator's note: the source reads «الشوك»; the verse is usually cited as «ترى الثور فيها مدخل الظل رأسه».]
2- Allusion (taʿrīḍ) in His saying «قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي». What is said about allusion has preceded. Their aim here was to allude that they were more entitled to prophethood than he, and that had Allah wished to place it in anyone He would have placed it in them. These people claimed to overcome Nūḥ in argument from two angles: first, that the followers are the lowest, neither an example nor a model; second, that they, besides that, did not deliberate in following him nor think deeply about the truth of what he brought, but rushed into it impromptu, without thought or deliberation.

dervis-irab:29-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِطارِدِ): الطرد is driving away; تطارد الأقوال is bringing some sayings to bear upon others.
(تَزْدَرِي): الازدراء is contempt and finding fault; it is the iftiʿāl form from الزراية. One says زريت عليه when you found fault with him, and أزريت به when you fell short [in his due] [Translator's note: the source prints «أزرت»]. The poet said:
رأوه فازدروه وهو خرق ... وينفع أهله الرجل القبيح
ولم يخشوا مقالته عليهم ... وتحت الرغوة اللبن الصريح
(They saw him and despised him, though he is generous — and an ugly man may benefit his people; they did not fear what he might say against them, yet beneath the froth lies pure milk.)

* I'rab:
(وَيا قَوْمِ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مالًا): conjoined to what preceded; لا is negating, أسألكم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), عليه is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and مالا is a second object. (إِنْ أَجرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ): إن is negating, أجري is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the yāʾ of the speaker in genitive construct, إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and على الله is the khabar (predicate). (وَما أَنَا بِطارِدِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is the Ḥijāzī ما, operating like ليس, أنا is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and طارد is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما; الذين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause). (إِنَّهُمْ مُلاقُوا رَبِّهِمْ وَلكِنِّي أَراكُمْ قَوْماً تَجْهَلُونَ): إنّ and its noun, ملاقوا is its khabar and ربهم a muḍāf ilayhi. ولكني: the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction, لكنّ and its noun, and the clause أراكم is its khabar; the kāf is the first object of أراكم, قوما is a second object, and the clause تجهلون is a naʿt (adjective). (وَيا قَوْمِ مَنْ يَنْصُرُنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنْ طَرَدْتُهُمْ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): conjoined to what precedes it; من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, the clause ينصرني is the khabar, and من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينصرني. إن is conditional, and طردتهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); it is a past verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then who will help me?". أفلا تذكرون: the hamza is for the interrogative of denial; either it enters on something implied, its implied form being "Do you command me to drive them away, and do you not reflect?", or it has been brought forward from a later position, the original being فألا تذكرون, the hamza being placed before the fāʿ because it has the right to the head of the clause; the establishment of this has preceded. تذكرون is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped, its original being تتذكرون. (وَلا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي خَزائِنُ اللَّهِ وَلا أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negating, أقول is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "I", لكم is attached to أقول, عندي is an adverb of place attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and خزائن الله is a postponed mubtadaʾ. ولا أعلم الغيب is conjoined to عندي خزائن الله, i.e. "nor do I say to you that I know the unseen". But a problem with this conjoining is that it would entail its being governed by the negated أقول, so that the implied form becomes "nor do I say: I do not know the unseen", which is not correct. The safer course is that it be conjoined to لا أقول, not to what is said, and then the problem disappears. I do not know how this escaped al-Zamakhsharī and other great parsers. (وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ): also coordinated with the first لا أقول; إنّ, its noun and its khabar are the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl).
(وَلا أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِي أَعْيُنُكُمْ لَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ خَيْراً): also conjoined; للذين is attached to أقول, and the clause تزدري أعينكم is the ṣila; لن is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future, and يؤتيهم is accusative by it; the hāʾ is the first object of يؤتي, الله is the fāʿil, and خيرا is the second object of يؤتي. (اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنِّي إِذاً لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar, بما is attached to أعلم, and في أنفسهم is the ṣila of the relative noun; إنّ and its noun, إذن is a particle of answer and requital without governing effect (muhmal), the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and من الظالمين is the khabar of إنّ; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there is a lofty device among the devices of badīʿ, namely combination with division (al-jamʿ maʿa al-taqsīm): the speaker combines two or more things and then divides what he has combined. In these verses there is a refutation of the doubts they raised when they said «ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين». He answered them with a reply that can be traced back to the doubts they raised, as though he were saying: "If your denying me any superiority relates to the superiority of wealth and rank, I have not claimed it, nor have I told you that the treasuries of Allah are with me, that you should dispute with me about it and deny it." Abū Firās gazed at this sky in his saying:
إنّا إذا اشتد الزما ... ن وناب خطب واد لهم
ألفيت حول بيوتنا ... عدد الشجاعة والكرم
للقا العدا بيض السيو ... ف وللندى حمر النعم
هذا وهذا دأبنا ... يودى دم ويراق دم
(When times grow hard and a calamity strikes and darkens, you will find around our houses the equipment of courage and generosity: white swords for meeting the enemy, and red camels for bounty. This and that are our custom: blood-money is paid, and blood is shed.)

dervis-irab:32-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الجدال) and المجادلة: confronting [the opponent] with what twists the opponent away from his position, by an argument or a specious doubt. It is الجدل, i.e. strong twisting. One says جدل الحبل: he twisted the rope; a twisted halter (زمام مجدول) is الجديل. They say: "as though in the halter", "one of the daughters of Jadīl" [a famous stallion]. طعنه فجدّله: he thrust at him and threw him down on الجدالة, which is the earth. [The poet] said:
قد أركب الآلة بعد الآله ... وأترك العاجز بالجداله
(I ride one hard state after another, and leave the feeble man lying on the ground.)
The falcon is called أجدل because it is among the strongest of the hunting birds. They say: "If they stand still, they are palaces (جوادل); and if they pass by, they are falcons (أجادل)", i.e. if they stand [Translator's note: the source prints «وفقن» for «وقفن»], they are palaces, and if they pass by, they are falcons. Al-Aʿshā said:
في مجدل شيّد بنيانه ... يزلّ عنه ظفر الطائر
(In a fortress whose structure is built high, from which the bird's talon slips.)
Among the figurative usages: امرأة مجدولة الخلق, a woman of slender build; درع مجدولة and جدلاء, i.e. a firmly made coat of mail; عمل على جديلته, he acted according to his nature on which he was "twisted"; استقام جدول القوم, when the people's affair became orderly, like a stream (جدول) when its flow is steady and continuous. A Bedouin looked at the pilgrims' caravan proceeding in succession and said: "As for the pilgrims, their stream has become straight." From following the derivation of this root it becomes clear that every word whose first and second radicals are jīm and dāl indicates strength, twisting and firmness. Thus جدب المكان جدوبة, and جدب and أجدب, the opposite of أخصب (to be fertile) — and it is not hidden what hardship and affliction there is in that for those whose land becomes barren. الجدث is the grave, and among their sayings: «شر الأحداث، نزول الأجداث» ("the worst of events is descending into graves"). جدح السويق واللبن بالمجدح: he stirred the gruel and milk with the مجدح, which is a stick with two crosspieces at its head with which it is stirred until mixed. أرسلت السماء مجاديح الغيث (the sky sent down the rain-stirrers); المجاديح is the plural of المجدح, i.e. al-Dabarān [the star], whose rain-season (nawʾ) is abundant. In the ḥadīth of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: "I have sought rain with the مجاديح of the sky," by which he meant seeking forgiveness. رجل مجدود: a fortunate man; and there is nothing in this world stronger than the workings of الجَدّ (with fatḥa on the jīm), i.e. fortune; and الجِدّ (with kasra) is effort and toil. مشى على الجادّة: he walked on the main road; امشوا على الجوادّ, which is the plural of الجادة. أجدّ المسير and جدّ: he hastened the journey. [The poet] said:
أشوقا ولما يمض لي غير ليلة ... فكيف إذا جدّ المطي بنا عشرا
(Longing already, when only one night has passed for me? Then how will it be when the mounts hasten with us for ten?)
جدره: he called him from behind the wall (الجدار). He is جدير بكذا, i.e. strong enough to undertake it. Zuhayr said:
بخيل عليها جنّة عبقرية ... جديرون يوما أن ينالوا فيستعلوا
(With horses ridden by men like jinn of ʿAbqar, worthy one day to attain and rise high.)
جُدر الصبي and جُدّر: the boy had smallpox; he is مجدور الوجه and مجدّر. Among the witty verses of Ibn al-Muʿtazz:
بي قمر جدّر لما استوى ... فزاده حسنا وزالت هموم
أظنه غنى لشمس الضحى ... فنقطته طربا بالنجوم
(I love a moon [a beauty] who caught smallpox when he reached his prime, which only increased his beauty and dispelled cares; I think he sang to the morning sun, and in delight she dotted him with stars.)
جدع أنفه وأذنه: he cut off his nose and his ear, so he is مجدوع; when it becomes a permanent quality, one says أجدع, feminine جدعاء. جادع صاحبه: he quarrelled with his companion and reviled him; جدّعه, when he said to him "جدعا لك" (may you be mutilated). جدف الملّاح السفينة: the sailor propelled the ship with the oar (المجداف). Aʿshā Hamdān said:
لمن الظّعائن سيرهنّ تزحّف ... عوم السفين إذا تقاعس تجدف
(Whose are the travelling women whose march creeps along, like the floating of ships, when they lag, propelled by oars?)
خفق الطائر بمجدافيه: the bird flapped its two "oars", i.e. its wings, which are its strength. الجدا and الجدوى are a gift — and how strong it is! استجديته: I asked him [for a gift]; جدوته and اجتديته are like it. [The poet] said: جدوت أناسا موسرين فما جدوا ... ألا الله أجدوه إذا كنت جاديا
(I asked wealthy people for gifts and they did not give; rather, ask Allah when you seek a gift.)
One of our early men of letters perceived this root and the secret of the conjunction of the jīm and the dāl, and enumerated it in verse, which we cite below:
عظمة والقطع حظ جدّ ... والاجتهاد ضد هزل جدّ
وجانب وجاء جمعا جدّ ... واسم لما بين الكلا من بئر
أمّ أب وأمّ أمّ جدّه ... ومصدر الشيء الجديد جدّه
مدينة أي بالحجاز جدّه ... والضمّ والكسر لشط النهر
للنبت والحائط قيل جدر ... وللنبات قيل أيضا جدر
وجمع جدر أي جدار جدر ... وآفة الأطفال داء الجدري
والسنة الشديدة الجداع ... أما الجدال فاسمه جداع
والكلأ الذّاوي هو الجداع ... كذا وضيم الكلم المضرّ
الفتل والصرع وعود جدل ... والصدر بالفتح وكسر جدل
جمع جديل أي زمام جدل ... وجمع جدلاء لدرع الكر
(A didactic poem listing the meanings of words from the jīm-dāl roots: جدّ for greatness, cutting off, fortune and seriousness; جدّة for grandmother, newness, and the city of Jidda in the Ḥijāz; جدر for plants and wall, and smallpox (الجدري); جداع for a hard year, for disputation and for withered pasture; جدل for twisting, throwing down, and the plural of جديل (halter) and of جدلاء (coat of mail).)
This is truly remarkable.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا يا نُوحُ قَدْ جادَلْتَنا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدالَنا): قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); يا is a vocative particle, and نوح is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), جادلتنا is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فأكثرت is conjoined to جادلتنا, and جدالنا is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ): the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ, i.e. "if you are truthful, then bring us". بما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, the clause تعدنا is the ṣila (relative clause), and the returning pronoun is omitted. It is also correct for ما to be maṣdar-forming, i.e. "[bring] your promise to us". إن كنت من الصادقين is a condition whose apodosis is indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring us"; من الصادقين is the khabar (predicate) of كنت. (قالَ إِنَّما يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ إِنْ شاءَ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ): إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), يأتيكم is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi, به is attached to يأتيكم, and الله is the fāʿil; إن شاء is a condition and its verb, and the apodosis is omitted. وما: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), ما is the Ḥijāzī ما, أنتم is its noun, and بمعجزين is its khabar, accusative in position, because of the redundant preposition. (وَلا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negating, and ينفعكم نصحي is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; إن أردت is a condition and its verb, أن with what is in its domain is the object of أردت, and لكم is attached to أنصح. إن كان is likewise a condition and its verb; الله is the noun of كان, the clause يريد is the khabar of كان, and أن يغويكم — أن with what is in its domain — is the object of يريد. The explanation of the succession of the two conditions is that the apodosis of the second condition, namely إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم, is what is indicated by His saying لا ينفعكم نصحي, and the second condition with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first. The detail of that and its meaning will come in the section of Benefits. (هُوَ رَبُّكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ربكم the khabar; إليه is attached to ترجعون; ترجعون is in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): أم is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa); يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the clause افتراه is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl). (قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرامِي وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُجْرِمُونَ): إن is conditional, and افتريته is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), عليّ is a fronted khabar and إجرامي a postponed mubtadaʾ; أنا is a mubtadaʾ and بريء the khabar, مما is attached to بريء, and the clause تجرمون is the ṣila.

* Benefits:
When two conditions and one apodosis come together in speech, the second condition is made a condition within the first, so the apodosis does not take place unless the second condition is fulfilled and exists in reality before the first exists. The parallel to this verse among the questions of the jurists is the saying: "You are divorced if you drink if you eat." This is known as the question of one condition intervening upon another. What is transmitted is that if she drank and then ate, he does not break his oath [i.e. she is not divorced], and if she ate and then drank, he breaks it. The commentators have established concerning the verse that when one condition comes upon another, the second is prior to the first in meaning, even though it is later in wording; the implied form is: "My advice will not benefit you, if Allah intends to lead you astray, if I wish to advise you." Al-Bayḍāwī said: "Thus is the construction of the speech: if Allah intends to lead you astray, then if I wish to advise you, my advice will not benefit you for that reason. And if someone said: 'You are divorced if you enter the house if you speak to Zayd,' and she entered and then spoke to Zayd, she is not divorced."
Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī:
They mentioned that when one condition intervenes upon another, e.g. "if you eat, if you drink, you are divorced", the stated apodosis belongs to the earlier of them, and the apodosis of the second is omitted, indicated by the first condition and its apodosis (that is, the first condition and its apodosis are later in meaning, since it is the indication of the apodosis), as they said concerning the apodosis that comes after an oath and a condition. For this reason the precise jurists said of the example mentioned that she is not divorced until she does first what was mentioned later and later what was mentioned first, because the implied form then is "if you drink, if you eat, you are divorced". All of this is good, but they counted among it His saying, Exalted is He: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم — and this is questionable, since two conditions do not follow in succession with an apodosis after them, as in the example and as in the poet's saying:
إن تستغيثوا بنا إن تذعروا تجدوا ... منّا معاقل عزّ زانها كرم
(If you seek our help, if you are frightened, you will find in us strongholds of might adorned by generosity.)
and the saying of Ibn Durayd:
فإن عثرت بعدها إن وألت ... نفسي من هاتا فقولا: لا لعا
(And if I stumble after this — if my soul escapes from this one — then say: may he not rise again.)
For in the noble verse no apodosis is mentioned; rather, what is the apodosis in meaning of the first condition precedes the two conditions, so it ought to be implied next to it, and the original would be: "If I wish to advise you, my advice will not benefit you, if Allah intends to lead you astray." As for implying the apodosis after the two of them and then further implying it as brought forward next to the condition, there is no justification for it.
And he said in al-Durar: When one condition enters upon another, sometimes it is by conjunction and sometimes without. If it is by conjunction, Ibn Mālik stated without qualification that the apodosis belongs to the first of them because it comes first [Translator's note: the source prints «لا ولهم», evidently a misprint for «لأولهما»]. Others distinguished: if the conjunction is with the wāw, the apodosis belongs to both, because the wāw is for simple combination, e.g. "If you come to me and if you treat me well, I will treat you well"; if the conjunction is with أو, the apodosis belongs to one of them, because «أو» is for one of two things, e.g. "If Zayd comes or if Hind comes, then honour him or honour her"; and if the conjunction is with the fāʾ, the apodosis belongs to the second, and the second with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first. If it is without conjunction, the apodosis belongs to the first of them, and the second condition restricts the first, as it would be restricted by a ḥāl (circumstantial) occurring in its place, as in the verse cited as evidence. When the interrogative enters upon a condition, it is reported from Yūnus that the apodosis belongs to the interrogative because it precedes the condition, by analogy with the question of an oath preceding a condition, e.g. "If Zayd stands, will you stand?"
A useful summary:
Clarification of the question: in this form there are two conditions, and there is only one thing fit to be the apodosis. So it must be one of the following. Either it is made the apodosis of both together — and there is no way to that, because of what it entails of two governors combining on a single governed word, which is invalid.
Or it is made the apodosis of neither — and there is no way to that, because of what it entails of bringing what has no place in the speech and leaving what has a place, which is futile. [Translator's note: the source prints «الآيتان», a misprint for «الإتيان».]
Or it is made the apodosis of the latter rather than the first — and there is no way to that, because it would entail that the second with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first, so the linking fāʾ would have to be brought, and there is no fāʾ. So the fourth division is determined, namely that it is the apodosis of the first rather than the second, and the first with its apodosis is the indication of the apodosis of the second. So the original is: "If you drink, then if you eat, you are divorced." If he said these words, she would not be divorced until she drank and then ate; and likewise what has its meaning.

dervis-irab:36-39.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الابتئاس): grief with abasement. [The poet] said:
ما يقسم الله اقبل غير مبتئس ... منه واقعد كريما ناعم البال
(Whatever Allah apportions, accept it without grieving over it, and sit honourably with a mind at ease.)
It is the iftiʿāl form from البؤس. In al-Mukhtār: "ولا تبتئس, i.e. do not grieve and do not complain; المبتئس is one who is averse and grieved."
