(الْفُلْكَ): the majority hold that it is with ḍamma on the fāʾ and sukūn on the lām; it is also said that one says فُلُك with two ḍammas. Al-Raḍī, in his commentary on al-Shāfiya, pointed to the possibility that [the form] with two ḍammas is the original and that the ḍamma on the first with sukūn on the second is perhaps a lightening of it, like عُنْق; he dealt at length with its justification [Translator's note: the source prints «بصمتين» for «بضمتين»]. In al-Qāmūs: "الفلك, with ḍamma, is the ship; it is masculine, and it is used for the singular and the plural; or الفلك which is a broken plural of الفلك which is a singular." This very statement occurs also in al-Ṣiḥāḥ and al-ʿUbāb. Ibn Barrī said: the correct form is "the فلك which is a singular", because if you make الفلك a singular it is masculine only, and if you make it a plural it is feminine only. It is also said that الفلك is made feminine even when it is singular — He, Exalted is He, said: «قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين» — and on that view no correction is needed.

* I'rab:
(وَأُوحِيَ إِلى نُوحٍ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ): the wāw is a conjunction, أوحي is a passive past verb, and أنّ with what is in its domain is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause لن يؤمن is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ, إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), من is the fāʿil (agent) of يؤمن, and the clause قد آمن is the ṣila (relative clause). (فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ بِما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ): the fāʿ is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تبتئس is jussive by لا, بما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تبتئس, the clause كانوا is the ṣila, and the clause يفعلون is the khabar of كانوا. (وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا وَوَحْيِنا): اصنع is conjoined to what preceded, الفلك is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and بأعيننا is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "guarded by Our eyes"; its literal sense is "bound up with [Our eyes]", as though Allah had eyes with him guarding him. ووحينا is conjoined to أعيننا. (وَلا تُخاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِنَّهُمْ مُغْرَقُونَ): لا is prohibitive and تخاطبني is jussive by it, the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, في الذين is attached to تخاطبني, and the clause ظلموا is the ṣila. وإنهم مغرقون: إنّ, its noun and its khabar, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for not addressing [Him]. (وَيَصْنَعُ الْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّما مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُ): a narration of a past state, so the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), brought for this purpose; the implied form is "and he set about making the ship". الفلك is a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and كلما is an adverb of time containing the sense of condition, attached to سخروا منه; what is said about كلما has preceded. مر عليه ملأ is a verb and its fāʿil, عليه is attached to مرّ, and the clause سخروا منه has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (قالَ إِنْ تَسْخَرُوا مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنْكُمْ كَما تَسْخَرُونَ): قال is a past verb, إن is conditional, تسخروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and منا is attached to تسخروا; the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), إنّ and its noun, and the clause نسخر منكم is the khabar of إنّ. كما تسخرون: the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); it has had many parallels before. (فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ عَذابٌ يُخْزِيهِ): the fāʿ is resumptive, and سوف is a particle that transfers the verb from the present to the future. The difference between it and the sīn is that سوف has a sense of postponement (taswīf), which is attaching the soul to matters that may happen. تعلمون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. من may be a relative in the position of the accusative by تعلمون, تعلمون having the sense of recognising, so it takes one object; or it may be interrogative, and it is likewise a mafʿūl bihi; or تعلمون may be [a verb] of certainty, so that the second object is omitted. يأتيه is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi, عذاب is the fāʿil, and the clause يخزيه is a naʿt of عذاب. (وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ): يحل is conjoined to يأتيه, عليه is attached to يحل, عذاب is the fāʿil and مقيم a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «انهم مغرقون» the statement comes in the denial-countering form (inkārī), emphasised with إنّ, to reinforce the speech and to treat the listener as one who hesitates; because for the alert soul it is a likely occasion for hesitation over the content of the statement and for the burden of seeking it. So He said first: ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا, i.e. "do not call on Me, O Nūḥ, to ward off the punishment from them"; then He said: انهم مغرقون, because the speech is a likely occasion for Nūḥ to hesitate as to whether some harm would befall them — indeed, as to whether they would be drowned — considering His earlier saying واصنع الفلك. So He presented the statement emphasised and said: they are sentenced to drowning.

dervis-irab:40-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فارَ): الفور is boiling, and its origin is rising. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "فار الماء يفور فورا: the water gushed and flowed; فارت القدر فورا وفورانا: the pot boiled." [Translator's note: the source prints «فوراتا» for «فورانا».] From it comes their saying فعل ذلك من فوره, i.e. before it subsided [immediately], and شرب فورة العقار, which is its froth and what boils up from it.
(التَّنُّورُ): it is said that its measure is tafʿūl [تنوور], the first wāw being changed into a hamza because it has ḍamma, then dropped for lightness, and then the nūn doubled as compensation for what was dropped; Thaʿlab said this. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said its measure is faʿʿūl. It is also said to be foreign, and the well-known view is that it is among the words in which the language of the Arabs and that of the non-Arabs agree, like الصابون (soap). He said in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: التنور is the oven in which bread is baked, and its maker is تنّار; [it is also] the face of the earth, every place where water gushes forth, and the gathering place of the valley's water. Al-Tāj followed it by saying: it is said that it is so in all languages. Al-Layth said: التنور is common to every tongue. Abū Manṣūr said: this indicates that the noun is originally foreign, and the Arabs Arabised it, so it became Arabic on the pattern faʿʿūl. Then it is said that it is a known oven, so the speech is literal; and it is said to be figurative, the meaning of their saying فار التنور being "anger intensified", just as they say حمي الوطيس ("the oven grew hot") when fighting intensifies, and فار قدر القوم ("the people's pot boiled") when their war intensifies. The poet said:
تفور علينا قدرهم فنديمها ... ونفثؤها عنا إذا حميها غلا
(Their pot boils over against us, and we calm it, and cool it off from us when its heat boils up.)
(الاثنان): the explanation in the reading of Ḥafṣ with tanwīn, «ومن كلٍّ زوجين اثنين», is that the two are a pair of mates (زوجان). He, Exalted is He, said «ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين»; the woman is the زوج of the man and the man is her زوج; and it may be said of two: they are a زوج. Labīd said:
من كل محفوف يظلّ عصيّه ... زوج عليه كلة وقرامها
(From every [howdah] draped [with cloth], whose poles are shaded by a pair [of coverings] upon it: a canopy and its curtain.)
The meaning of the verse: the howdahs are draped with cloths, and their sticks are under the shade of their cloths. The pronoun after القرام [Translator's note: the source prints «والمضر» for «والمضمر»] refers to the sticks or to the canopy.

* I'rab:
(حَتَّى إِذا جاءَ أَمْرُنا وَفارَ التَّنُّورُ): حتى is connected with His saying واصنع الفلك بأعيننا, i.e. until this time, so it is a particle of limit and of the genitive. إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time, and the clause جاء أمرنا is in the position of the genitive by construct, and the clause وفار التنور is conjoined to the clause جاء أمرنا. (قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيها مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. احمل is an imperative verb, فيها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) احمل, من كل is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from زوجين, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of it, زوجين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and اثنين is a naʿt for emphasis and reinforcement, as He said: «لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين». (وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ): أهلك is conjoined to زوجين; إلا is a particle of exception and من is a connected excepted item, and the clause سبق عليه القول is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَمَنْ آمَنَ وَما آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ): ومن آمن is conjoined to أهلك. وما: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negating; آمن is a past verb, معه is an adverb attached to آمن, إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and قليل is the fāʿil (agent) of آمن. (وَقالَ ارْكَبُوا فِيها بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْراها وَمُرْساها): the wāw is a conjunction, قال is a past verb, the clause اركبوا فيها is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl), and فيها is attached to اركبوا. باسم الله is a fronted khabar (predicate) and مجراها a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is a ḥāl from the wāw or the hāʾ, i.e. "embark in it naming Allah", or "saying: in the name of Allah". مرساها is conjoined to مجراها; they are two mīm-maṣdars (maṣdar mīmī), the first from جرى, hence مَجرى, and the second from أرسى, hence مُرسى with ḍamma on the mīm. Both were also read with ḍamma, as mīm-maṣdars as well. They may also be nouns of time or place, i.e. "the time of its sailing and its anchoring", with بسم الله a ḥāl, i.e. "seeking blessing by the name of Allah", and the two adverbs attached to this omitted element; so it is of the type خفوق النجم ("at the setting of the star") and مقدم الحاج ("at the arrival of the pilgrims"). There are other views of the parsers here, which we have passed over. (إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), غفور is the first khabar of إنّ and رحيم the second khabar of إنّ. (وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ فِي مَوْجٍ كَالْجِبالِ): a ḥāl from something omitted, i.e. "so they embarked in it, while it sailed with them"; it may also be resumptive (mustaʾnafa). هي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تجري is the khabar, بهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, في موج is attached to تجري, and the kāf is a naʿt of موج. (وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, and نادى نوح ابنه is a verb, a fāʿil and an object. وكان: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), كان is a defective past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir), implied as "he", referring to the son, namely Kanʿān, and في معزل is the khabar of كان.
(يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا وَلا تَكُنْ مَعَ الْكافِرِينَ): يا is a vocative particle and بنيّ is the one addressed (munādā), in genitive construct to the yāʾ of the speaker. Its original form has three yāʾs: the first is the yāʾ of the diminutive, the second the yāʾ of the word [its third radical], and the third the yāʾ of the speaker. The yāʾ of the speaker was dropped for lightness, and the yāʾ of the diminutive was assimilated into the lām (third radical) of the word. It is read with kasra on the yāʾ and with fatḥa. Whoever read it with kasra made the kasra indicate the dropped yāʾ; and whoever read it with fatḥa intended the construct, just as he intended it in his saying يا بنيِّ when he gave kasra to the yāʾ that is the lām of the word — as though he said يا بنيّي, keeping the yāʾ of the construct [Translator's note: the source prints «باء الاضافة» for «ياء الإضافة»], then replaced the kasra with fatḥa and the yāʾ with alif, so that it became يا بنيّا, then dropped the alif just as the yāʾ had been dropped. Both readings are among the seven. اركب is an imperative verb, معنا is an adverb attached to اركب, لا is prohibitive, تكن is a defective imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its noun latent, implied as "you", and مع الكافرين is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar. (قالَ سَآوِي إِلى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الْماءِ): the clause سآوي is the speech reported by "say", إلى جبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آوي, the clause يعصمني is a naʿt of جبل, and من الماء is attached to يعصمني. (قالَ لا عاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ): لا is the lā of generic negation, عاصم is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and اليوم is an adverb attached to أمر الله, because it has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Better than that is that the khabar of «لا» is omitted, because when it is known, as in this place, Banū Tamīm always omit it and the people of the Ḥijāz frequently omit it. For when he said سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء, Nūḥ said to him: لا عاصم, i.e. "there is no protector in existence"; and اليوم is accusative by an implied verb indicated by عاصم, i.e. "there is no protector who protects today from the command of Allah", with من أمر a preposition and its genitive noun attached to that omitted verb. It is not permissible for اليوم to be accusative by his saying لا عاصم, nor for «من أمر الله» to be attached to it, because the noun of لا would then be "lengthened" (muṭawwal), and when it is lengthened it must have tanwīn and be declined. [Alternatively,] من أمر الله is the khabar of لا. إلا is a particle of exception or of restriction. The exception is either connected, so that من is the excepted item and the clause رحم the ṣila; or disconnected, with إلا in the sense of لكن, من a mubtadaʾ, the clause رحم the ṣila, and the khabar omitted, its implied form being "he is the one protected". It is useful to cite here what Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "His saying, Exalted is He, لا عاصم اليوم has three views. The first is that it is an active participle in its normal sense; on this view His saying إلا من رحم has two views: first, it is a connected exception, with من رحم meaning 'the one who has mercy', i.e. there is no protector except Allah; second, it is disconnected, i.e. but whoever Allah has mercy on is protected. The second view is that عاصم means معصوم ('protected'), like ماء دافق meaning مدفوق ('poured'); on this view the exception is connected, i.e. except whoever Allah has mercy on. The third is that عاصم means 'possessed of protection', as a relational form, like حائض and طالق; on this view too the exception is connected. As for the khabar of لا, it is not permissible for it to be اليوم, because an adverb of time cannot be the predicate of a concrete entity; rather, the khabar is من أمر الله, and اليوم is governed by من أمر الله. Nor is it permissible for اليوم to be governed by عاصم, since if it were, it would have tanwīn." The author of al-Intiṣāf put forward fine words, which we cite below: "The possible interpretations here are four: no protector except one who has mercy; no protected one except one shown mercy; no protector except one shown mercy; and no protected one except one who has mercy. The first two are exceptions from the same genus, and the latter two exceptions from a different genus, so they are disconnected." (وَحالَ بَيْنَهُمَا الْمَوْجُ فَكانَ مِنَ الْمُغْرَقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, حال is a past verb, بينهما is attached to حال, and الموج is the fāʿil; فكان is conjoined to حال, the noun of كان is latent, and من المغرقين is the khabar of كان.

dervis-irab:44-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البلع) is well known. Its verb has kasra or fatḥa on the second radical — بلِع and بلَع — both reported by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: بلعت الطعام بلَعا, of the pattern تعب; [one says of] water and saliva بلْعا with sukūn on the lām; and بلعته بلعا, of the pattern نفع, is a dialectal form; also ابتلعته. Among the figurative usages of this verb: أبلعني ريقي ("let me swallow my saliva"), i.e. give me respite so that I may speak or act.
Al-Zamakhsharī said in Asās al-Balāgha: I said to one of my teachers: "Let me swallow my saliva," and he said: "I have let you swallow the two rivers [the Tigris and Euphrates]."
(الاقلاع): removing a thing from its root so that no trace of it is seen. One says:
أقلعت السماء, when its rain has gone so that nothing of it remains; and أقلع عن الأمر, when he abandoned the matter completely.
(غِيضَ): in the passive, since it is used both intransitively and transitively. الغيض is diminution, and its verb is intransitive and transitive. Of the intransitive is His saying, Exalted is He, «وما تغيض الأرحام», i.e. diminish; and of the transitive is the verse we are dealing with, because a verb is not made passive without the mediation of a preposition unless it is transitive by itself. In al-Mukhtār: غاض الماء: the water lessened and sank away, of the pattern باع; انغاض is like it; غيض الماء: that was done to it; غاضه الله is both transitive and intransitive, and أغاضه الله also; غيّض الدمع تغييضا: he lessened the tears and held them back. One says: غاض الكرام, i.e. the noble became few, and فاض اللئام, i.e. the base became many.
(الْجُودِيِّ): a mountain in the land of al-Jazīra on which the ship came to rest at the end of the flood.

* I'rab:
(وَقِيلَ: يا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي ماءَكِ وَيا سَماءُ أَقْلِعِي): the wāw is a conjunction, قيل is a passive past verb, يا is a vocative particle, and أرض is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ابلعي is an imperative verb, the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), and ماءك is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ويا سماء أقلعي is conjoined to يا أرض ابلعي. (وَغِيضَ الْماءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ): clauses conjoined one to another. Of their secrets, what astonishes minds will come under Rhetoric. (وَقِيلَ: بُعْداً لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ): بعدا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "and it was said: may they be far removed, a removal"; so it is a maṣdar in the sense of an imprecation against them. للقوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, the implied form being "my wish" or the like; or to قيل, i.e. "this saying was said for their sake" [Translator's note: the source prints «لأجهلم», a misprint for «لأجلهم»]. الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are such varieties of eloquence and marvels of fluency as bewilder the mind and astonish the intellect. We shall present the most important devices that catch the eye and attract the gifted, so that they may follow their example and weave on their pattern.

1- Equivalence (al-musāwāt):
We begin with the device that concerns the verse as a whole. They defined it as the wording being equal to the meaning, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it. It is among the greatest chapters of eloquence; indeed, it is eloquence itself, as one describer described an eloquent man, saying: "His descriptions were moulds for his meanings"; and as al-ʿAttābī said: "Words are bodies and meanings are souls." It is the distinguishing mark of every language. Émile Faguet said in describing Victor Hugo: "Hugo is among the immortals, because what is immortal is beauty of style" — and beauty of style is the fit between word and meaning. The verse we are dealing with is the best example of this equivalence. For He, Glorified is He, wished to relate this part of the story in the most concise and most eloquent wording, and so He brought it with words and clauses arranged according to what took place, in forms that neither exceed their meanings nor fall short of them [Translator's note: the source reads «لا تفصل عن معانيها لا وتقصر عنها», evidently for «لا تفضل عن معانيها ولا تقصر عنها»]. If it is said: the word «القوم» is superfluous and prevents the verse from being described as equivalent, because if it were removed the speech would stand without it, so that one could say «وقيل بعدا للظالمين» — I say:
The speech cannot do without it. That is because, since He said at the beginning of the story «وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه», and after that said «ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون», the word القوم came at the end of the story, and He described them by wrongdoing, so that the end of the speech returns upon its beginning.

2- Returning the end upon the beginning (radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā al-ṣadr):
This is the second device of this verse. And so that it be known that the people who perished in the flood are those who used to mock Nūḥ, and that they therefore deserved punishment — lest a weak-minded person imagine that the flood, because of its generality, may have destroyed those who did not deserve destruction — Allah, Glorified is He, made known that those who perished are the ones mentioned before, together with what they used to do to His Prophet of the mockery by which they deserved destruction; and that they are the ones He described by wrongdoing, whose drowning He promised His Prophet, and concerning whom He forbade him to address Him. This was in order to remove that possibility, so that it would be known that Allah, Glorified is He, fulfilled for His Prophet what He had promised him, and destroyed the wrongdoing people whom He had mentioned and described earlier and whose drowning He had promised.

3- Allusive brevity (al-ishāra):
The third device of this verse is the device of ishāra, whose discussion has preceded. Qudāma defined it, saying: it is that a few words indicate many meanings, so that the indication of the words is like a gesture of the hand or a sign with the eyebrow and the eye, which indicates by a single quick movement many things that would take up long expressions. Among its examples in the verse we are dealing with is His saying «وغيض الماء»: the sinking away of the water indicates that the supply of water from the earth's springs and the sky's rain had been cut off; were it not for that, the water would not have sunk away.
4- Indirect expression (al-irdāf):
As for the fourth device, it is a marvellous device of its kind. It is that the speaker intends a meaning and does not express it by the word coined for it, nor by an allusive word indicating many meanings, but by a word that is a consequence (ridf) of the specific meaning and follows it, close to the word of the meaning as the one riding pillion is close to the rider. Here it is in His saying, Exalted is He, «وقضي الأمر», whose literal reality is: "and whoever Allah decreed to perish perished, and whoever He decreed to be saved was saved". He turned from this literal expression to the word of irdāf for the sake of concision, and to draw attention to the fact that the perishing of the one who perished and the salvation of the one saved came about by the command of one who commands and is obeyed, and the decree of one whose decree is not repelled. Command requires one who commands; its being decreed indicates the power of the one who commands it; and the obedience of the one commanded indicates the power and dominion of the one who commands; and that fear of His punishment and hope of His reward urge obedience to the one who commands. None of this is obtained from the specific word.
Moreover, among the examples of irdāf in poetry is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لو كنت حشو قميصي فوق نمرقها ... سمعت للجن في غيطانها زجلا
(Had you been the stuffing of my shirt upon its saddle-cushion, you would have heard the jinn clamouring in its hollows.)
By "the stuffing of my shirt" he means himself. He says: were you in my place, beneath my clothes and upon the cushion of my she-camel — on which the rider rests his thigh — you would have heard the din of the jinn and their voices in the low ground of these distant deserts, because they are the haunt of the jinn, being far from humans. The Arabs make a distant place the dwelling of the jinn, to make it seem fearsome and to express desolation in it.
5- Precaution (al-iḥtirās):
The fifth device in this verse is iḥtirās. Its definition is that the speaker brings a meaning against which an objection could be directed, and he perceives that at the moment of composing, and so includes in the original speech what frees it from that. Among its examples is His saying, Exalted is He, in it: «وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين». For when He, Glorified is He, reported the destruction of those destroyed by the flood, He followed it with an imprecation against those who perished and described them by wrongdoing, so that it would be known that all who perished deserved the punishment and merited it — as a precaution against a weak-minded person who might imagine that the destruction, in its generality, included someone who did not deserve punishment. When He imprecated against those who perished, it was known that everyone who perished deserved destruction, because it has been established by proof that He is just, so He imprecates only against those who deserve the imprecation. And after imprecating against them, He described them by wrongdoing; for if they were not wrongdoers, His statement would be subject to falsity, and His statement is exalted above that. So this imprecation and this description came as a precaution against what was supposed to be imagined. Iḥtirās appears beautifully [Translator's note: the source prints «جملا», read «جميلا»] in poetry; among it is the famous saying of Ṭarafa:
فسقى ديارك غير مفسدها ... صوب الربيع وديمة تهمي
(May your abodes be watered — without ruining them — by the spring downpour and steadily pouring rain.)
His saying "without ruining them" is a precaution against the effacing of their landmarks and the obliterating of their traces. Abū al-Ṭayyib inclined to it often; he said:
ويحتقر الدنيا احتقار مجرب ... يرى كل ما فيها، وحاشاك، فانيا
(He despises the world with the contempt of one experienced, who sees everything in it — far be it from you — as perishing.)
His saying "far be it from you" is a precaution against [the one addressed] being included among all who are in it.
And also his saying:
إذا خلت منك حمص لا خلت أبدا ... فلا سقاها من الوسمي باكره
(When Ḥimṣ is empty of you — may it never be empty! — may the early autumn rain not water it.)
His saying "may it never be empty" is a precaution against its being imagined as an imprecation against it.

6- Excellence of sequence (ḥusn al-nasaq):
The sixth device of this wondrous verse is the device of nasaq. It consists in the speaker bringing words in prose, or verses in poetry, in succession, cohering together soundly and pleasingly, not faultily and offensively. The verse from beginning to end is among the examples of this device: the clauses follow one another, coordinated one upon another by the wāw of coordination, in the order that eloquence requires. For He, Glorified is He, began with the most important, since what was intended was the release of the people of the ship from their prison, and that would not come about or be possible except by the receding of the water from the earth. Therefore He began with the earth and commanded it to swallow, and second with the sky and commanded it to cease, lest the people of the ship be harmed by it. Then He reported the sinking away of the water when the earth's water had gone and the sky's water had stopped. Then He said «وقضي الأمر», i.e. whoever the Pen had dried upon [decreeing] his destruction perished, and whoever [Divine] knowledge had foreordained to be saved was saved. This is the reality of the miracle and the essence of the sign, and it must be known to the people of the ship; and their knowledge of it is not possible until after they leave it, and their leaving depends on what preceded. Therefore eloquence required that this clause come as the fourth of the clauses. Likewise the ship's settling on al-Jūdī, i.e. its settling on the place where it settled, a settling with no movement, so that its traces would remain a sign for those who come after its people. He turned from the word استقرت to the word استوت, because of the swerving and tilting that استقرار may admit, while استواء indicates straightness and absence of deviation. In this lies the reassurance of the people of the ship, their security after fear, and the calming of their alarm. Had its settling been merely a settling, such that movement could not be ruled out with it, their state in enduring movement, and the agitation and pounding of their hearts, would have been the same whether it was sailing or stopped. Then finally He said «وبعدا للقوم الظالمين»; this is an imprecation required by precaution against one who thinks that the drowning, because it covered the earth, may have destroyed someone who did not deserve punishment. So He imprecated against those who perished and described them by wrongdoing, so that it would be known that the destruction covered only those who deserved punishment and no others — a precaution against this possibility.

7- Comparison (al-tanẓīr):
The seventh device in it is the device of tanẓīr. Ibn al-Athīr spoke about it in his book al-Istidrāk under the name of weighing poets against each other to show which of them is the better; it is closer to criticism than to the devices of badīʿ. Its definition is that a person compares two pieces of speech, either agreeing in meaning or differing in meaning, to show which of them is the better. The verse we are dealing with treats the story of the flood, which contains many complications, resolutions and lessons; if you compare it with other stories, you will find it lofty above all of them, in its exhaustive coverage of all that occurred in it and all that arose.

8- Verbal congruence (al-munāsaba al-lafẓiyya):
Between ابلعي and اقلعي; it resembles the congruence that came in His saying «لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم» in Sūrat Yūnus.
9- Incomplete paronomasia (al-jinās al-nāqiṣ):
Between ابلعي and اقلعي. Some call it al-muḍāraʿa. It is of various kinds, among them that one letter differs in the two words after the rest of the letters agree. Like it is His saying, Exalted is He, «وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه». The Prophet ﷺ said to a man whom he heard reciting boastfully — and it is also said that he asked him about his lineage — and he said:
إني امرؤ حميري حين تنسبني ... لا من ربيعة آبائي ولا مضر
(I am a man of Ḥimyar when you trace my lineage; my forefathers are not of Rabīʿa nor of Muḍar.)
The Prophet ﷺ said: "That, by Allah, is more ignoble for your ancestry (ألأم لجدك), more humbling for your cheek (أضرع لخدك), lesser for your number (أقل لعدك), and further for you from Allah and His Messenger."

10- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq):
The tenth device is ṭibāq, for He set the sky against the earth.

11- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra):
The eleventh device is the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) present in calling the earth and the sky with what a discerning animate being is called with, in the form of urging, and in turning to them with address from among all creatures — that is His saying يا أرض and يا سماء — and then commanding them with what beings of discernment and reason are commanded with, in His saying ابلعي ماءك واقلعي, by way of indicating the immense power [of Allah]. Swallowing [Translator's note: the source prints «البلغ» for «البلع»] is an expression for the earth's absorbing the water [Translator's note: «تغدير» in the source, probably for «تغوير»] and drinking it into its belly, borrowed for this meaning from an animal's swallowing, i.e. gulping down its food and drink. Swallowing is the effect of the attracting faculty on what is eaten, because of the complete resemblance between them, namely going to a hidden resting place. Moreover, it is the contextual clue (qarīna) for the implicit metaphor in the water, i.e. the borrowing of water for nourishment, the common factor being the earth's being strengthened by water in producing vegetation, [like] the eater's being strengthened by food.

12- Loose metonymy (al-majāz al-mursal):
That is in His saying «يا سماء», for the literal sense is "O rain of the sky, cease". The relation in this majāz is causality, because the water is the cause of the rain [Translator's note: so the source; the sense intended is presumably that the sky is the source of the rain], or locality, because [the sky] is its locus by virtue of the clouds gathering in it. The attribution of the water to the earth is also majāz, likening its connection with it to the connection of a possession with its owner. There is another subtle point in it, namely drawing attention to this water arising from the earth as well, not only from the sky, as indicated by His saying, Exalted is He, «وفار التنور».

13- Representation (al-tamthīl):
It is that the speaker intends a meaning and does not express it by its specific word, nor by the words of ishāra or irdāf, but by a word somewhat more remote than the word of irdāf, fit to be a likeness of the specific word — because a likeness does not resemble its counterpart in every respect; if two likenesses were alike in every respect they would be one. The detail of this device has preceded. [It is] in His saying «واستوت على الجودي», whose literal reality is: "and it sat upon that place". He turned from the literal sense to representation because of the intimation in استواء of a firm sitting, with no swerving or tilting, no movement and no agitation.

14- Concision (al-ījāz):
He, Glorified is He, related the story with its wording comprehensive, so that He omitted nothing of it, in the briefest expression and with words that are not lengthened.
15- Anticipation (al-tashīm):
It is that what precedes in the speech indicates what comes later, or vice versa. The tashīm in the verse is that the beginning of the verse calls for its end.

16- Refinement (al-tahdhīb):
Because the individual words are described with the qualities of beauty, and every word has easy points of articulation and is free from dissonance, strangeness and violation of the rule.

17- Firm placement (al-tamkīn):
Because the verse-ending (fāṣila) is settled in its place, at rest in its position, neither unsettled nor out of place.

18- Smooth flow (al-insijām):
It is the determining of words with ease and sweetness, together with the grandeur that the setting requires and the situation demands.

19- Anticipatory preparation (al-irṣād):
It is that the reader guesses the verse-ending before pronouncing it.

20- Harmony of word with meaning (iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā):
It is what practitioners of the art call the pairing of words, so much so that Anatole France, the French writer, said: "Between words there is a Catholic marriage." Every word is such that no other is fit in its place. Abū Tammām was keen on this device in his poetry; listen to his saying:
وفي الكلمة الوردية اللون جؤذر ... من الانس يمشي في رقاق المجاسد
رمته بخلف بعد أن عاش حقبة ... له رسفان في قيود المواعد
(And in the rose-coloured canopy is a human fawn walking in fine saffron-dyed garments; she struck him with a broken promise, after he had lived a long while shuffling in the fetters of her promises.) [Translator's note: the source has «الكلمة»; the word in Abū Tammām's verse is usually «الكِلّة» (canopy).]
The fāʿil (agent) of رمته is in verses that came earlier. This is a matter for which words are incapable of finding limits; it is something that taste alone perceives, in the manner of Voltaire's saying:
"Your taste is your teacher."

21- The repeated metaphor:
If you add to what preceded that metaphor occurs in it in two places — namely the metaphor of swallowing and that of ceasing — you obtain twenty-one devices.
Moreover, some rhetoricians added the following to these devices:
1- Among them: that He, Exalted is He, did not state explicitly the agent of غيض, قضي and قيل, just as He did not state explicitly the speaker of قيل at the beginning of the verse, nor did He state explicitly who levelled the ship [Translator's note: so the source, «بمن سوى السفينة»]; drawing attention to the fact that such tremendous matters cannot be conceived of as occurring except from One All-Powerful whose essence cannot be fathomed and an Irresistible One who is not overcome, so that the mind does not go to any agent other than Him, nor does the imagination stretch to any range beyond this range. It is also said, concerning the reason for turning away from stating the agent explicitly, that it indicates that these matters are too trivial for Allah, Exalted is He, for Him to attribute them explicitly to His power.
2- Among them: the singular of الماء, intimating that this water did not come about from the gathering of waters and their multiplying, but is a single kind that came about by His power, Exalted is He, all at once.
3- Among them: the singular of «أرض», indicating that this water covered the whole, so that the whole became like one thing in view of this covering; and also the singular of «سماء», indicating that what is meant by it here is the direction of height whose extent is not fathomed, not the celestial bodies.
4- Among them: the allusion (taʿrīḍ) with which the speech was concluded, drawing the attention of those who follow their path and incline as they inclined in denying the messengers to the fact that what befell them — a drowning that covered the entire world — was only because of their wrongdoing and their going to extremes in obstinacy and persistence in denial.
5- Among them: mentioning the object of ابلعي, lest, by its omission, the swallowing extend generally to the seas and still waters, as the station of Majesty would require.
6- Among them: putting the command to the earth before the sky, because the flood began from it.
Moreover, al-Sakkākī mentioned other secrets, which we have passed over because of the artificiality in them, which may turn the matter into its opposite.

* Benefits:
1- The emphasising maṣdar may stand in place of its verb, whether used or disused, so that the verb cannot be mentioned with it. It is of two kinds: a- one that has no verb at all from its root, e.g. ويلك, ويحك, بله الأكف and سبحان الله.
b- one that has a verb in use from its root; this is of two kinds. One kind occurs in request, namely what comes in an invocation for good or its opposite — the first like سقيا and رعيا, the original being سقاك الله سقيا ("may Allah water you") and رعاك الله رعيا ("may Allah protect you") — or what comes as a prohibition or a command, e.g. قياما لا قعودا ("stand, do not sit"), and likewise the specifying kind, e.g. «فضرب الرقاب», i.e. "then strike the striking of necks". The other kind occurs in statements, e.g. حمدا وشكرا لا كفرا ("praise and thanks, not ingratitude"). These have kinds mentioned in the lengthy works. The preposition and its genitive noun that occur after the likes of سقيا لك and بعدا للقوم الظالمين are attached to an omitted element that serves as clarification, the implied form being "my wish is for them", and they are not attached to the maṣdar. So the likes of سقيا لك are, on this view, two clauses.

2- The lām of clarification (lām al-tabyīn):
It is fitting here to present a brief summary of this lām, which has greatly occupied the grammarians, though they have not given it its due in explanation. It is of three kinds:
a- One that distinguishes the object from the agent. Its criterion is that it comes after a verb of wonder or an elative noun conveying love or hatred. You say: ما أحبني and ما أبغضني ("how loving / how hating I am"); if you say: لفلان, then you are the agent of the love or hatred and he is its object; and if you say:
إلى فلان, the matter is the reverse.
b and c: one that clarifies agency not confused with objecthood, and one that clarifies objecthood not confused with agency. What accompanies each of them is either not known from what precedes it, or known but its clarification is made afresh to strengthen and emphasise the clarification. The lām in all of this is attached to an omitted element. An example of the one clarifying objecthood: سقيا لك and جدعا لك. This lām is not attached to the two maṣdars nor to their implied verbs, because these are transitive by themselves, as are the maṣdars; nor [Translator's note: the source prints «و "لا"», read «ولا»] is it with its genitive noun a naʿt of the maṣdar, attached to [a notion of] being established — because the verb is not described, and likewise what stands in its place. Rather, it is a lām that clarifies the one for whom or against whom the invocation is made, the implied form being "my wish is for you". An example of the one clarifying agency:
تبا لزيد and ويحا له, which mean "he lost" and "he perished"; in that case Zayd is the agent, and the lām is attached to an omitted element: "my wish is existing for Zayd".

* Vocabulary:
(فَطَرَنِي): Allah created (فطر) the creation, and He is the Fāṭir of the heavens, i.e. their originator; and "iftaṭara al-amr" means he originated the matter. «Every child is born upon the fiṭra», i.e. upon the innate disposition. "He split (faṭara) this well"; "Allah caused the tree to burst forth (faṭara) with leaves, so it burst forth (infaṭara) and split open (tafaṭṭara) with them"; "the earth split open (tafaṭṭarat) with vegetation"; "the hand and the garment split (tafaṭṭarat)", i.e. cracked; "the camel's canine tooth emerged (faṭara)"; "the woman kneaded (faṭarat) the dough"; and "this is speech that breaks (yufṭir) the fast", i.e. invalidates it.
(مِدْراراً): al-midrār means abundant in flowing, like al-mighzār ("abundantly flowing"). It is not given the feminine form even though it describes a feminine noun, for three reasons. First, what is meant by "the sky" (السماء) is the clouds or the rain, so it was made masculine according to the sense. Second, miʿfāl is a form of intensification, in which the masculine and the feminine are alike, as in ṣabūr (very patient) and shakūr (very thankful). Third, the feminine ending (hāʾ) was dropped from miʿfāl on the pattern of relational adjectives (nisba). In al-Qāmūs: "the sky poured (darrat) with rain, a pouring (darran and durūran), so it is midrār."
(الناصية): the place where the hair grows at the front of the head. The hair growing there is also called nāṣiya, after its location. "Naṣawtu al-rajul" means I took hold of his forelock. Its lām (final radical) is a wāw, and it is also said "nāṣāt", the yāʾ being changed to alif. Seizing by the forelock is an expression for overpowering and subduing, even if no forelock is actually seized; for this reason, when they showed favour to a captive, they would cut off his forelock.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى عادٍ أَخاهُمْ هُوداً): conjoined to the story of Nūḥ. The conjoined element is omitted, i.e. "and We sent to ʿĀd", so this is a conjunction of sentences, not of single words, because of the length of the separation. عاد is the name of a tribe; it is declined fully (ṣarf) because the clan (ḥayy) is intended; had the tribe (qabīla) been intended, it would be a diptote. أخاهم is the object of the omitted verb أرسلنا; "their brother" is meant in terms of lineage. هودا is a badal or an ʿaṭf bayān; the subtle difference between badal and ʿaṭf bayān will come in the section on Benefits. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ): اعبدوا الله: an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object. ما is negative; لكم is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; إله is genitive in form, nominative in position, because it is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and غيره is an adjective of إله according to its position (nominative); the genitive is also allowed as an adjective according to the form, and it has indeed been read that way.
(إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَرُونَ): إن is negative; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; مفترون is the khabar of أنتم. (يا قَوْمِ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً): لا is negative; أسألكم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent and a first direct object; عليه is a ḥāl; أجرا is the second direct object.
(إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): إن is negative; أجري is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; على الذي is the khabar; the clause فطرني is the ṣila; the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction (the discussion of this construction has already preceded); تعقلون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. (وَيا قَوْمِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً): استغفروا ربكم: an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; ثم توبوا إليه is conjoined to استغفروا; يرسل is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the response to a request; السماء is a direct object; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مدرارا; and مدرارا is a ḥāl from السماء (the reason for not giving it the feminine form has already been mentioned). (وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلى قُوَّتِكُمْ وَلا تَتَوَلَّوْا مُجْرِمِينَ): ويزدكم is conjoined to يرسل; the kāf is the first direct object and قوة the second direct object; إلى قوتكم is an adjective, and إلى here means "with" (maʿa); ولا تتولوا: لا is prohibitive and تتولوا is jussive by لا; مجرمين is a ḥāl from the wāw. (قالُوا يا هُودُ ما جِئْتَنا بِبَيِّنَةٍ): يا is a vocative particle; هود is the one addressed, a single proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ما is negative; جئتنا is a verb, an agent and a direct object; ببينة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئتنا, so the bāʾ is for transitivity (taʿdiya); it may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, i.e. "settled" or "furnished with" a clear proof.
(وَما نَحْنُ بِتارِكِي آلِهَتِنا عَنْ قَوْلِكَ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī mā, نحن is its subject (ism); the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; تاركي is genitive in form, accusative in position as the predicate of ما; and عن قولك is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تاركي, as if he had said "we do not abandon our gods, issuing from your saying"; it is also possible that عن is causal, the meaning being "we are not abandoners of our gods because of your saying", in which case it is attached to تاركي itself. (وَما نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī mā, نحن is its subject; لك is attached to مؤمنين; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and مؤمنين is genitive in form, accusative in position as the predicate of ما.
(إِنْ نَقُولُ إِلَّا اعْتَراكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنا بِسُوءٍ): إن is negative; نقول is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; إلا is a particle of restriction; the clause اعتراك is the object of نقول, i.e. it is accusative through an omitted maṣdar, which maṣdar is accusative by نقول, i.e. "except our saying: 'ʿtarāka...'"; the kāf is a direct object; بعض آلهتنا is the agent; and بسوء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اعتراك. The meaning is "we say nothing except our saying that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil." More on this point will come in the section on Benefits.
(قالَ: إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ): inna and its ism; its hamza is given a kasra after قال; the clause أشهد is its khabar; واشهدوا is an imperative verb; أن (with fatḥa on the hamza) and what is in its scope is the object of اشهدوا or of أشهد الله, the matter being one of tanāzuʿ (competition of two governors for one object), and the discussion of tanāzuʿ will come in the section on Benefits; then أن with its ism and khabar; مما is attached to بريء; the clause تشركون is the ṣila; ما may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "from your associating (others with Allah)". (مِنْ دُونِهِ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ لا تُنْظِرُونِ): من دونه is a ḥāl; فكيدوني: the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); كيدوني is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the deletion of the nūn, the wāw being the agent, the nūn for protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ (dropped for lightness) a direct object; جميعا is a ḥāl; ثم is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تنظرون is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the omitted yāʾ (dropped for lightness) is a direct object. (إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ): إني: inna and its ism; the clause توكلت is its khabar; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to توكلت; ربي is a badal or an adjective; and ربكم is conjoined to ربي.
(ما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِناصِيَتِها): ما is negative; من is a redundant preposition; دابة is a mubtadaʾ (the indefinite is permissible as a mubtadaʾ because it is preceded by a negation); إلا is a particle of restriction; هو is a mubtadaʾ; آخذ is the khabar; and بناصيتها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آخذ. (إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): inna and its ism; على صراط is its khabar; and مستقيم is an adjective.
(فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تولوا is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped, the original being تتولوا, and it is the protasis, jussive by the deletion of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; قد is a particle of certainty; أبلغتكم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; ما is the second direct object; the clause أرسلت is the ṣila; به is attached to أرسلت; and إليكم is a ḥāl. (وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ وَلا تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئاً): a resumptive sentence, and for this reason it is nominative and not conjoined to the apodosis; although it has also been read jussive, by position, which is correct and beyond reproach; ربي is the agent and قوما the direct object; غيركم is an adjective of قوما; ولا تضرونه is conjoined to يستخلف; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. some harm. (إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ): inna and its ism; على كل شيء is attached to حفيظ, and حفيظ is the khabar of inna. (وَلَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُنا نَجَّيْنا هُوداً وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا): لما is a temporal adverbial particle (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) attached to نجينا, or a connective; جاء أمرنا: a verb and an agent; نجينا هودا: a verb, an agent and a direct object; والذين is conjoined to هود; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; معه is an adverb of place attached to آمنوا; برحمة is attached to نجينا; and منا is an adjective of رحمة.
(وَنَجَّيْناهُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ): ونجيناهم: a verb, an agent and a direct object; من عذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجيناهم; and غليظ is an adjective of عذاب.
(وَتِلْكَ عادٌ جَحَدُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَعَصَوْا رُسُلَهُ): the wāw is resumptive and the sentence is resumptive, brought to sum up the abominations committed by the people of ʿĀd; تلك is a mubtadaʾ; عاد is a badal or an ʿaṭf bayān; the clause جحدوا is the khabar of تلك; or you may make تلك عاد a mubtadaʾ and khabar and then begin a new sentence; بآيات is attached to جحدوا; ربهم is a muḍāf; and عصوا رسله: a verb, an agent and a direct object. (وَاتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ): واتبعوا is conjoined to جحدوا; أمر is a direct object; كل is a muḍāf ilayhi; جبار is a muḍāf ilayhi of كل; and عنيد is an adjective of جبار. (وَأُتْبِعُوا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): واتبعوا is conjoined to what precedes; it is a passive past verb, the wāw being the deputy agent; في هذه الدنيا is attached to أتبعوا; الدنيا is a badal of the demonstrative; لعنة is the second direct object; and يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "they were followed"; al-Fārisī allowed يوم القيامة to be conjoined to the position of هذه, because the phrase في هذه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتبعوا and so is itself a governor in the position of accusative, and there is nothing to prevent conjoining a time to الدنيا, since it is an adverb of place, both sharing in being adverbials. (أَلا إِنَّ عاداً كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ): ألا is a particle of alerting; inna and its ism; كفروا is a verb and an agent; and ربهم is accusative by removal of the preposition; you may also make it accusative as a direct object by embedding in كفروا the meaning of جحدوا. (أَلا بُعْداً لِعادٍ قَوْمِ هُودٍ): ألا is a particle of alerting, an emphasis of the first; the i'rab of بعدا has already been given, and the meaning of the lām and its attachment were given in detail at a nearby place, so renew your acquaintance with it; قوم is a badal or a conjoined element, and هود is a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of Allah the Exalted: «He said: I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free of what you associate» (قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا اني بريء مما تشركون). He said "I call Allah to witness (أشهد الله) and bear witness (واشهدوا)" and did not say "and I call you to witness" so that it would be balanced with it and of the same meaning, because his calling Allah to witness his freedom from polytheism is sound and established, whereas his calling them to witness is nothing but making light of their religion and an indication of how little he cares about them; therefore he departed in it from the wording of the first, because of the difference between the two, and it was brought in the form of the imperative, like the saying of a man to one between whom and himself the bond of affection has dried up: "Bear witness against me that I do not love you", in mockery of him and contempt for his condition. This is from one aspect. From a second aspect, the form of a report admits nothing but the reporting that the calling to witness has occurred from him; so since his calling Allah to witness was actual and verified, it was expressed in the form of a report, because it is a sound and established calling to witness; and in their case it was expressed in the imperative form, which includes making light of their religion, and that is what he intended in this context. From a third aspect, he departed to the imperative form from the form of a report only to distinguish between his address to Allah the Exalted and his address to them, by expressing the address to Allah the Exalted in the form of a report, which is more exalted, nobler and more reverent toward the one addressed than the imperative form.

* Benefits:
1- The difference between ʿaṭf bayān and badal:

Points of similarity between them:
The points of similarity between ʿaṭf bayān and badal are four:
1- That in it there is clarification of the second, as in the badal.
2- That it occurs with inert nouns (non-derived), like the badal.
3- That its wording may be the wording of the first, by way of emphasis.
4- Both are followers (tābiʿ).

Points of difference between them:
The points of difference between them are:
1- The badal is what is intended by the predication, not the substituted-for (mubdal minhu), whereas the ʿaṭf bayān is not what is intended; rather, what is intended by the predication is the antecedent, and the ʿaṭf bayān is brought only to clarify it and to reveal what is meant by it.
2- Everything that may be an ʿaṭf bayān may be a badal of the whole from the whole, unless it is impossible to dispense with it or with its antecedent, in which case it must be an ʿaṭf bayān. An example of the impermissibility of dispensing with the follower is your saying: "Fāṭima, Ḥusayn her brother came", for if you deleted "her brother" (أخوها) from the speech the construction would be corrupted. [Translator's note: the example sentence is given as in the source.]
3- That ʿaṭf bayān proceeds according to what precedes it in its definition, which is not the case with the badal, because it is permissible to substitute an indefinite for a definite and a definite for an indefinite, and that is not permissible in ʿaṭf bayān. [Translator's note: the source reads "what is before it" literally "ما قلبه", apparently a misprint for "ما قبله"; translated as "what precedes it".]
4- That the badal may be with an overt noun or a pronoun, and likewise the substituted-for, and that is not permissible in ʿaṭf bayān; and the badal may be other than the first, as in your saying "Zayd was robbed, his garment", whereas ʿaṭf bayān is never other than the first. [Translator's note: the source has "سلب زيد ثوبه" with the verb in the active form as printed.]

2- The second benefit:
«إن نقول إلا اعتراك»: إن is a particle of negation attached to نقول, negating all saying except one saying, namely their saying "some of our gods have afflicted you with evil"; the implied form is "we say no saying except this statement". The verb indicates the maṣdar, the adverbial of time or place, and the ḥāl, and it is permissible to mention the verb and then make an exception, from what it indicates, of the maṣdars, adverbials and ḥāls it indicates. So اعتراك is excepted from the maṣdar indicated by نقول, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: «We shall not die except our first death» (فما نحن بميتين إلا موتتنا الأولى), where موتتنا is accusative as an exception, because it is excepted from the kinds of death indicated by his words بميتين. [Translator's note: the quoted verse is cited as in the source, with the wording «فما نحن بميتين».] An example of this among adverbials is His saying: «And on the Day He gathers them, as if they had not tarried except an hour of the day» (ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار), where ساعة is an exception from the times indicated by لم يلبثوا. An example of this among ḥāls is His saying: «Humiliation is struck upon them wherever they are found, except with a rope from Allah» (ضربت عليهم الذلة أينما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله); the implied form is: "humiliation is struck upon them in all circumstances wherever they are found, except holding fast to a rope", i.e. to a covenant from Allah.

3- The third benefit: tanāzuʿ (competition of governors):
It is when two inflected verbs, or two nouns resembling them, come first, and after them comes a governed word that is demanded by each of them, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: «Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper» (آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا). You may make either of the two governors act on the mentioned noun as you wish: if you make the second act, it is for its nearness, and if you make the first act, it is for its precedence. If you make the first act on the overt noun, you make the second act on its pronoun, whether nominative or not, as in: "He stood and they sat, your two brothers", "he strove and I honoured them both, your two brothers", "he stopped and I greeted them both, your two brothers", "I honoured, so he explained", and "I honoured, so Khālid thanked me". Some of the grammarians permitted its omission if it is not a nominative pronoun, as in the poet's verse:
بعكاظ يعشي الناظرين إذا هم لمحوا شعاعه
(At ʿUkāẓ it dazzles the onlookers when they glimpse its radiance.)
And if you make the second act on the overt noun, you make the first act on its pronoun if it is nominative, as in "the two stood and sat, your two brothers", "they both strove and I honoured your two brothers", "they both stopped and I greeted your two brothers", and from it is the poet's verse:
جفوني ولم أجف الأخلاء إنني ... لغير جميل من خليلي مهمل
(They were harsh to me, though I was not harsh to my friends; indeed I am neglected by my friend without any good.)
And if its pronoun is not nominative, you omit it, as in "I honoured and your two brothers explained", "I honoured, so Khālid thanked me", "I honoured and Saʿīd honoured me", and "I passed by and ʿAlī passed by me".
There are other rulings for tanāzuʿ, to be consulted in the longer books of grammar.

dervis-irab:84-95.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ): the imperfect of جَرَمَ, of the pattern ضَرَبَ, as in al-Mukhtār. It takes one object or two, and its meaning is "to bring upon you / to earn for you".
(رَهْطِي): al-rahṭ is a man's group. It is also said that al-rahṭ and al-rāhiṭ denote fewer than ten men, and that al-rahṭ, al-ʿuṣba and al-nafar apply only to men. Al-Zamakhsharī said: from three to ten; it is also said, up to nine. Its plural is arhuṭ and arhāṭ, and the plural of the plural is arāhiṭ. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: al-raḥṭ and al-rahṭ are a man's people and tribe, and a number gathered from three to ten that includes no woman; it has no singular from its own word, and its plural is arhuṭ and arhāṭ, with the plural of the plural arāhiṭ and arāhīṭ. When a number is added to al-rahṭ, what is meant is the individual and the person, as in عشرون رهطا, "twenty persons". One says ذوو رهط, "those who are gathered together".
(ظِهْرِيًّا): cast behind your backs, not watched over by you. Ẓihrī is relative to al-ẓahr (the back); the kasra is one of the alterations that occur in relative adjectives (nisba), whereas the analogical form would have a fatḥa on the ẓāʾ. They said imsī for ams with a kasra on the hamza, and dahrī for al-dahr with a ḍamma on the dāl. The alterations that befall the nisba will come in the section on Benefits. The word ẓahr has idioms in our language, which we give here in summary from the dictionaries: "They travelled by the road of the ẓahr", i.e. the desert road. "He read the book ʿalā ẓahr qalbihi or ʿalā ẓahr lisānihi", i.e. from memory. "He gave him ʿan ẓahr yadin", i.e. initially, without recompense. "He is staying bayna ẓahrayhim, ẓahrānayhim and bayna aẓhurihim", i.e. in their midst and among most of them. "I saw him bayna ẓahrānay al-layl", i.e. between the night prayer and dawn. "He turned the back of the shield for him" (qalaba lahu ẓahra l-mijann), i.e. he changed toward him and became his enemy. "He turned the matter back to belly" (qalaba l-amra ẓahran li-baṭn), i.e. he thought it out thoroughly. "He killed him ẓahran", i.e. by treachery. "He eats ʿalā ẓahr yadī", i.e. I spend on him. This is among the rare and unusual features of our language. How beautiful is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
وضربنا الحديث ظهرا لبطن ... وأتينا من أمرنا ما اشتهينا
(We turned the conversation back to belly, and we did of our affair whatever we desired.)
(مَكانَتِكُمْ): al-makāna is either in the sense of al-makān (place), as one says makān and makāna, and maqām and maqāma; or it is a verbal noun from makuna, whence makīn.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ أَخاهُمْ شُعَيْباً قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ): It is the custom to open each story of this sūra with this sentence. This is the sixth story, and the i'rab of this sentence, word for word, has already been given.
(وَلا تَنْقُصُوا الْمِكْيالَ وَالْمِيزانَ إِنِّي أَراكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ): The wāw is a conjunction; lā is prohibitive; تنقصوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil; المكيال is mafʿūl bihi; والميزان is conjoined to المكيال; inna and its noun, and the clause أراكم is its khabar. The clause إني أراكم is a causal clause for the prohibition. (وَإِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ مُحِيطٍ): The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; the clause أخاف عليكم is its khabar; عذاب is mafʿūl bihi; يوم is muḍāf ilayhi; and محيط is naʿt. (وَيا قَوْمِ أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيالَ وَالْمِيزانَ بِالْقِسْطِ): أوفوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; المكيال is mafʿūl bihi; والميزان is conjoined to it; and بالقسط is ḥāl, i.e. "being just". (وَلا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْياءَهُمْ وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; lā is prohibitive; تبخسوا is an imperfect verb jussive by lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil; الناس is mafʿūl bihi; أشياءهم is a second mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "do not diminish their property for them". ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين is also conjoined, and مفسدين is ḥāl. (بَقِيَّتُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ وَما أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ): بقية الله is the mubtadaʾ, i.e. His provision that remains after the full measure and weight have been given; خير is the khabar; and لكم is attached to خير. In is conditional; كنتم is the protasis; مؤمنين is the khabar of كنتم; the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then the remainder of Allah is better". As for وما, the wāw is a conjunction and mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; أنا is its noun; عليكم is attached to حفيظ; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and حفيظ is genitive in form and accusative in position. (قالُوا: يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا): The hamza is for interrogation, and its sense is mockery and ridicule; صلاتك is the mubtadaʾ and the clause تأمرك is the khabar; an and what lies within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition and is attached to تأمرك, i.e. "commands you to leave". Mā is either relative or maṣdar, and in either case it is the object of "leaving"; the clause يعبد has no grammatical position in either case; and آباؤنا is the fāʿil. (أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي أَمْوالِنا ما نَشؤُا): Aw is a conjunction; and أن نفعل is an interpreted maṣdar conjoined to mā in both of its readings, so "leaving" governs it, i.e. "does it command you to impose on us the leaving of what our fathers worship, and the leaving of doing with our property what we wish?"
Ibn Hishām cited this verse in Mughnī al-Labīb, in the fifth chapter of the book, on the aspects from which objection may enter upon the one who parses. He said: "Some of these examples are ones in which the parsers went wrong, and they fell into error for this reason, and you will see that clearly. The first of them is the saying of the Exalted: «أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء». It comes to mind at once to conjoin أن نفعل to أن نترك, but that is false, because he did not command them to do with their property what they wish. Rather it is conjoined to «mā», so it is governed by "leaving", and the meaning is that we leave [and] that we do" — and so on until he says:
"The cause of this error is that the parser sees an and the verb in sequence with a conjunction between them." There is disagreement about aw: it is said that it has the meaning of wāw, and it is said that it keeps its normal sense of option, like its place in your saying "sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn".
And mā is a relative noun, the object of نفعل, and the clause نشاء is the ṣila.
(إِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ الْحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ): Either they meant to mock him to the utmost degree and so reversed the sense in order to jeer, or it is meant literally, and what he commands them to do does not agree with what characterizes him. Inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; أنت is the mubtadaʾ; الحليم الرشيد are its two khabars; and the sentence is the khabar of إنك. (قالَ: يا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَرَزَقَنِي مِنْهُ رِزْقاً حَسَناً): أرأيتم has already been explained as meaning "tell me", so it governs two objects, both of which are omitted here. The first is implied as "tell me", so the speaker's yāʾ is the first object, and the second is usually implied as an interrogative clause, i.e. "Shall I then adulterate my provision with what is unlawful through short-changing and cheating in measure?" In is conditional; كنت is kāna and its noun, and it is the protasis; على بينة is the khabar of كنت; من ربي is naʿt of بينة; the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the omitted second object. رزقني is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; رزقا is mafʿūl bihi or mafʿūl muṭlaq; and حسنا is naʿt. (وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخالِفَكُمْ إِلى ما أَنْهاكُمْ عَنْهُ): Mā is negative; أريد is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "I"; an and what lies within its scope is the object of أريد; إلى ما is attached to أخالفكم; the clause أنهاكم عنه is the ṣila; and the meaning is "I do not want to get ahead of you to your desires that I have forbidden you". One says خالفه إلى كذا when he goes after it while the other is turning away from it. (إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا الْإِصْلاحَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ): In is negative; أريد is an imperfect verb whose latent fāʿil is implied "I"; illā is a particle of restriction; الإصلاح is mafʿūl bihi; and mā is temporal, a ẓarf of time, attached to أريد. (وَما تَوْفِيقِي إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ): Mā is negative; توفيقي is the mubtadaʾ; illā is a particle of restriction; بالله is the khabar; عليه is attached to توكلت; إليه is attached to أنيب; and the two clauses are ḥāl. (وَيا قَوْمِ لا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقاقِي أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمْ مِثْلُ ما أَصابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ): لا يجرمنكم: lā is prohibitive; يجرمنكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive by lā; the kāf is its first object; شقاقي is the fāʿil; an and what lies within its scope is the second object of يجرمنكم; the kāf is the object of يصيبكم; مثل is the fāʿil of يصيبكم, and it is originally an adjective of an omitted fāʿil, i.e. "a punishment like"; mā is muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "like that which"; the clause أصاب is the ṣila; and قوم نوح is mafʿūl bihi. (أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صالِحٍ وَما قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِنْكُمْ بِبَعِيدٍ): أو قوم هود is conjoined to قوم نوح, and likewise قوم صالح. Mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; قوم is its noun; لوط is muḍāf ilayhi; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ببعيد; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and بعيد is genitive by the bāʾ in form and is, in position, the khabar of mā. بعيد is brought in the singular although it is a predicate about a plural, for one of several reasons: among them the omission of a muḍāf, implied as "the destruction of the people of Lūṭ is not far"; or on account of time, i.e. "at a distant time", or place, i.e. "at a distant place"; or because the form faʿīl is the same for masculine and feminine, as will come to us in the course of this comprehensive book. (وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّي رَحِيمٌ وَدُودٌ): واستغفروا ربكم is an imperative verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ثم توبوا إليه is conjoined to استغفروا; and inna with its noun and its two khabars.
(قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ ما نَفْقَهُ كَثِيراً مِمَّا تَقُولُ): Mā is negative; نفقه is an imperfect verb whose latent fāʿil is implied "we"; كثيرا is mafʿūl bihi; مما is naʿt of كثيرا; and the clause تقول is the ṣila. (وَإِنَّا لَنَراكَ فِينا ضَعِيفاً وَلَوْلا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْناكَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْنا بِعَزِيزٍ):
وانا: inna and its noun; the shifted lām; the clause نراك is the khabar of inna; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; فينا is ḥāl; and ضعيفا is a second mafʿūl bihi, because the seeing is by knowledge — even though it is reported that he was blind and had a lisp — for had it been said "we see you among us blind" it would not have been speech, since the blind man is blind among them and among others. Lawlā is a particle indicating the prevention of one thing by the existence of another; رهطك is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the lām links the apodosis of lawlā; the clause رجمناك has no position; mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; أنت is its noun; the bāʾ is redundant; and عزيز is its khabar. Parallels to this have already occurred many times. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَرَهْطِي أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ): The hamza is for rebuking, reproachful interrogation; رهطي is the mubtadaʾ; أعز is the khabar; and عليكم and من الله are attached to أعز. (وَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَراءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا): The wāw is circumstantial, with an implied qad, i.e. "while you have taken Him behind you"; اتخذ may take two objects, the first being the hāʾ and the second ظهريا, and وراءكم is attached to اتخذتموه or is a ḥāl from ظهريا; it may also take one object, so the hāʾ is its object and ظهريا is ḥāl. The wāw in اتخذتموه lengthens the ḍamma of the mīm. (إِنَّ رَبِّي بِما تَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ): Inna and its noun; بما is attached to محيط; the clause تعملون is the ṣila; and محيط is the khabar of inna. (وَيا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ): اعملوا is an imperative verb and a fāʿil; على مكانتكم is ḥāl, i.e. "while you are described by lofty standing and far-reaching ability"; and inna with its noun and khabar. (سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ عَذابٌ يُخْزِيهِ): Sawfa is a particle of futurity; تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn; the clause is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), and more of it will come in the section on Rhetoric. Man is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi of تعلمون, and this is preferable to making it interrogative, as some have parsed it, so as to be in harmony with the second man, which is relative by agreement; the clause يأتيه is the ṣila; the hāʾ is the object of يأتي; عذاب is the fāʿil of يأتي; and the clause يخزيه is naʿt of عذاب.
(وَمَنْ هُوَ كاذِبٌ وَارْتَقِبُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ رَقِيبٌ): ومن is a relative noun conjoined to the first man; it is a mubtadaʾ; كاذب is the khabar; the sentence is the ṣila; وارتقبوا is conjoined in sense; ارتقبوا is an imperative verb and a fāʿil; inna and its noun; معكم is a ẓarf attached to رقيب; and رقيب is the khabar of inna. (وَلَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُنا نَجَّيْنا شُعَيْباً وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا): The i'rab of its like has been given in full. (وَأَخَذَتِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ): الذين is a fronted mafʿūl bihi of أخذت; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila of the relative; and الصيحة is the fāʿil of أخذت. (فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دِيارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ): أصبح and its noun; جاثمين is its khabar; and في ديارهم is attached to جاثمين. (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها أَلا بُعْداً لِمَدْيَنَ كَما بَعِدَتْ ثَمُودُ): Ka-an is the lightened form, and its noun is omitted; the clause لم يغنوا is its khabar; فيها is attached to يغنوا; alā is a particle of alerting; بعدا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; لمدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, which has already occurred; كما is naʿt of بعد; and mā is maṣdar, i.e. "like the removal of Thamūd".

* Rhetoric:
1- Repetition (al-takrār):
Repetition occurs in this story in three respects, because he said "do not diminish the measure and the balance", and this is identical to the first, with only a change of expression, "do not cheat people of their things". The benefit in it is that, since they persisted in that ugly deed, emphatic stress was needed in forbidding it; repetition conveys intensity of concern for the matter. They were first forbidden the ugly thing they were engaged in, the shortening of measure and balance; then the command came to give full measure, stated in its own words, so that it would be more provoking and more inviting to the matter.
2- Explanatory resumption (al-istiʾnāf al-bayānī):
When the speech being delivered is more deserving of attention than what preceded it, and more worthy of drawing the ears to it, it is cut off from what precedes it by something that draws the attention to it. That is in the saying of the Exalted:
«ويا قوم اعلموا على مكانتكم اني عامل سوف تعلمون» [Translator's note: the source writes اعلموا, "know", here, whereas the verse reads اعملوا, "act", as quoted in the i'rab above.] The fāʾ that the context requires has been dropped so as to draw the listener's attention and notice to the fact that there is a question — "and what will come after that?" — and this is more effective in awe, because his saying "you will know" contains acts of vengeance and threat whose essence cannot be grasped and whose depth cannot be sounded.
Al-Zamakhsharī said concerning this omission: "What is the difference between including the fāʾ and leaving it out in sawfa?" He answered by saying: "Including the fāʾ is an overt connection by a particle laid down for connecting, and leaving it out is a hidden, implied connection by the resumption, which is the answer to an implied question, as if they had said: 'And what will happen if we act according to our standing and you act according to yours?' So it was said, 'You will know.' The strongest and most eloquent of the two connections is the resumption, because it is more perfect in the domain of eloquence and the inspiring of awe."

3- Allusion (al-taʿrīḍ):
In his saying "I am acting" there is an allusion, and reference to this art has already been made. He mentioned to them one of the two outcomes without mentioning the second, which is an allusion more eloquent than the explicit statement. A parallel to this occurred earlier in Sūrat al-Anʿām, where He said: «قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار». There He mentioned one of the two outcomes, because what was meant by that outcome was the good outcome, and He dispensed with mentioning its counterpart. In the verse of Hūd, however, He mentioned their outcome, namely «سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه», and dispensed with it in place of his own outcome. Sometimes his outcome is not mentioned, and it is then turned to the one addressed, as when you say to someone you are threatening: "You will know who is humiliated and who is punished", while you mean only the one addressed in both statements.

* Benefits:
The relative adjective (nisba) deviating from analogy:
The Arabs formed relative adjectives from many things and altered the word of the thing related to; this was used as the Arabs used it and nothing else is measured on it. The rules of the nisba are well known in the books of grammar; these nisbas simply came deviating from analogy. Among that is their saying badawī as a nisba to al-bādiya, whereas the analogy is bādī or bādawī. They said baṣrī, with a kasra on the bāʾ, as a nisba to al-Baṣra, whereas the analogy is a fatḥa. They said ṭāʾī, whereas the analogy is ṭayʾī. They said suhlī and dahrī with a ḍamma on the sīn and the dāl, whereas the analogy is suhlī and dahrī [Translator's note: as printed; the vowelling that distinguishes the analogical form from the one cited appears to have been lost in the source]. They said baḥrānī as the nisba to al-Baḥrayn and ṣanʿānī as the nisba to Ṣanʿāʾ. They divided this into nine categories, which we give in brief:
1- By alteration (taḥrīf) only, as their saying umawī with a fatḥa on the hamza as a nisba to Umayya with a ḍamma, and dahrī for the aged man.
2- By addition, as their saying marwazī as a nisba to Marw, and fawqānī, taḥtānī and rabbānī as nisbas to fawq, taḥt and rabb.
3- By deletion, as their saying badawī with deletion of the alif, and jalūlī, as nisbas to al-bādiya and Jalūlāʾ.
4- By deletion and alteration, as shatawī from shitāʾ.
5- By addition and alteration, as anāfī from anf.
6- By addition and deletion, as in rāzī as a nisba to al-Rayy.
7- By inversion (qalb), as in ṭāʾī, ṣanʿānī and rūḥānī as nisbas to Ṭayy, Ṣanʿāʾ and Rawḥāʾ.
8- By inversion and alteration, as in thawb ḥārī as a nisba to al-Ḥīra.
9- By preserving what deserves to be changed, as in umayyatī as a nisba to Umayya.

dervis-irab:61-68.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ): "He made you live there (ʿammarakum) and settled you (askanakum)", so the sīn and tāʾ are redundant; or "He made you inhabitants (ʿāmirīn) of it", so they are for transformation (ṣayrūra). This root has wide branches in the language, which we present in what follows: ʿamara yaʿmuru (like dakhala): "ʿamara the house with its people" means it was inhabited; ʿamara al-manzil means he dwelt in it, so it is maʿmūr; ʿamara al-dār means he built it, and the noun is al-ʿimāra; ʿamara bi-l-makān means he stayed in the place; and "ʿammarahu Allāh" means Allah made him live long. Also ʿamara yaʿmuru (like dakhala and ḍaraba), verbal nouns ʿumūran, ʿimāratan and ʿumrānan: the man ʿamara his house, i.e. kept to it; "ʿamartuhu kadhā" means I assigned it to him for the length of his life or my life (ʿumrā); "istaʿmarahu fī al-makān" means he made him inhabit it; and "istaʿmara Allāhu ʿibādahu fī al-arḍ" means He asked them to cultivate it. But in the modern period the word changed to the meaning of ominous colonialism (isti'mār), which is on its way to disappearance, and al-mustaʿmarāt (colonies) are what a state possesses in lands other than its own; this is a neologism, but it has become one of the current words expressing a widespread meaning, so there is no harm in accepting it. As for al-ʿumr with fatḥa on the ʿayn, it is life and religion, and in oaths one says "laʿamrī" and "laʿamru Allāh"; it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted, its implied form being "my oath", and the lām entering it is the lām of ibtidāʾ, not of oath, because an oath may not be introduced onto an oath; and you say "ʿamra Allāhi mā faʿaltu" with the accusative as a maṣdar. More about this root and the i'rab uses in it will come. Let us return to the verse at hand and say: the meaning of واستعمركم فيها is "He commanded you to cultivate it".
