The jurists divided cultivation into obligatory, recommended, permissible and disliked, the details being given in the longer works. It is related of Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān that at the end of his life he took up reviving land, and it was said to him, "What made you do that?" He said, "Nothing made me do it but the saying of the poet:
ليس الفتى بفتى لا يستضاء به ... ولا تكون له في الأرض آثار
(A young man is no young man by whom none is enlightened, and who leaves no traces upon the earth.)"
It is also said that the meaning is "He made you live long" from al-ʿumr, like istabqākum from al-baqāʾ ("He kept you alive"); and it is said that it is from al-ʿumrā, meaning "He gave you your dwellings for life (aʿmarakum) in it", so that He inherits them from you after your lifetimes have ended, or made you inhabitants of your dwellings, living in them for the span of your lives and then leaving them to others.
(فَعَقَرُوها): Qudār struck it on its legs and brought it down; then they slaughtered it and divided its meat. This Qudār is a well-known wretch, to whom Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā alluded in his Muʿallaqa when he described the ill omen of war and the harm it generates, saying:
فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم ... كأحمر عاد ثم ترضع فتتئم
(Then it will bear you boys, every one of them more ill-omened than the Red One of ʿĀd; then it will suckle and give birth to twins.)
He meant: war will bear you, from its midst, sons each of whom resembles in ill omen the "Red One of ʿĀd", who is the hamstringer of the she-camel, whose name is Qudār ibn Sālif; he meant the Red One of Thamūd, but he applied to him the name that was current for the second ʿĀd, who are the people of Thamūd. So there is no point in the claim of those who said that Zuhayr made a mistake.
(جاثِمِينَ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "the bird and the hare jathama yajthimu (like ḍaraba), jūthūman", which is like the kneeling (burūk) of a camel; the active participle is jāthim, and jaththām is intensive.
(لَمْ يَغْنَوْا): "they did not dwell"; in al-Mukhtār: "ghaniya bi-l-makān" means he dwelt in it.

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ): Then Allah, glorified be He, conjoined to that the story of Ṣāliḥ, which is the third story of the stories of the sūra, and the i'rab of these words has already been given verbatim in the story of Hūd.
(هُوَ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيها): هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أنشأكم is the khabar; من الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنشأكم; and واستعمركم فيها is conjoined to أنشأكم. (فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّي قَرِيبٌ مُجِيبٌ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; فاستغفروه: an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; ثم is a conjunction; وتوبوا إليه is conjoined to استغفروه; and inna with its ism and two khabars.
(قالُوا يا صالِحُ قَدْ كُنْتَ فِينا مَرْجُوًّا قَبْلَ هذا): قد is a particle of certainty; kāna and its ism; مرجوا is its khabar; فينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; قبل is an adverbial attached to مرجوا; and هذا is a muḍāf ilayhi. What is meant is: "You have disappointed our hope in you, for we used to discern in you signs that announced right guidance." (أَتَنْهانا أَنْ نَعْبُدَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا): the hamza is for denunciatory interrogation, in their claim; تنهانا is an imperfect verb with a latent agent and a direct object; أن and what is in its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, both attached to تنهانا; and آباؤنا is the agent of يعبد. (وَإِنَّنا لَفِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا تَدْعُونا إِلَيْهِ مُرِيبٍ): the wāw is resumptive; inna and its ism; the shifted lām; في شك is the khabar of إننا; مما is an adjective of شك; the clause تدعونا is the ṣila; نا is the object of تدعو; إليه is attached to it; and مريب is an adjective of شك. (قالَ: يا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي): the like of أرأيتم has appeared more than once; here it is suspended from acting (muʿallaqa) because there follows what has the right to the opening of the speech; إن is conditional; كنت is the protasis, the tāʾ being the ism of kāna; على بينة is the khabar of kāna; and من ربي is an adjective of بينة. (وَآتانِي مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنْ عَصَيْتُهُ): وآتاني is conjoined to كنت; the yāʾ is the first direct object; منه is a ḥāl; رحمة is the second direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; ينصرني is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object, and the clause is the khabar; the clause فمن ينصرني is the apodosis of إن; the second إن is conditional and عصيته is its protasis, its apodosis being omitted, indicated by the apodosis of the first, i.e. "so who will help me"; the interrogative here has the meaning of negation, as if he said "then I have no helper against Allah if I disobey Him". It was permissible to disregard (ilghāʾ) رأيت here only because it entered upon a sentence standing by itself, in that it conveys a benefit if separated from others. (فَما تَزِيدُونَنِي غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; تزيدونني is an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object; غير is a second direct object of تزيدونني. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the stronger view here is that it is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "something other than loss". (وَيا قَوْمِ هذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً): the wāw is a conjunction; هذه is a mubtadaʾ; ناقة الله is the khabar; لكم is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of آية, but was fronted; and آية is a ḥāl from ناقة الله, the governor in it being the verbal meaning indicated by the demonstrative. (فَذَرُوها تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ): فذروها: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ذروها is an imperative verb and a direct object; تأكل is the response to a request, and therefore jussive; and في أرض الله is attached to تأكل. (وَلا تَمَسُّوها بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذابٌ قَرِيبٌ): ولا تمسوها is conjoined to what precedes; لا is prohibitive; تمسوها is jussive by لا, the wāw being the agent and the hāʾ the direct object; بسوء is attached to تمسوها; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; the kāf is a direct object; عذاب is the agent; and قريب an adjective. (فَعَقَرُوها فَقالَ تَمَتَّعُوا فِي دارِكُمْ ثَلاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ): فعقروها: the fāʾ is a conjunction and عقروها is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; فقال is conjoined to عقروها; the clause تمتعوا, an imperative verb with its agent, is the reported speech; في داركم is a ḥāl; and ثلاثة أيام is an adverbial attached to تمتعوا. (ذلِكَ وَعْدٌ غَيْرُ مَكْذُوبٍ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; وعد is the khabar; and غير مكذوب is its adjective. مكذوب may be a maṣdar on the pattern of mafʿūl, like al-majlūd, al-maʿqūl, al-manshūr and al-maghbūn; and it may be a passive participle in the original sense, with two interpretations: one, "not lied about concerning it" (غير مكذوب فيه), then the preposition was omitted and the pronoun became attached as a latent nominative in the adjective; and the second, that the promise itself is made "not lied", because it has been fulfilled, and when it is fulfilled, it is true. (فَلَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُنا نَجَّيْنا صالِحاً وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or connective; جاء أمرنا: a verb and an agent; نجينا صالحا: a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position; والذين is conjoined to صالحا; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; and معه is an adverb of place attached to آمنوا. (بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ): برحمة is a ḥāl, i.e. "accompanied by mercy", and منا is its adjective; ومن خزي is attached to an omitted element indicated by what precedes, i.e. "and We saved them from the disgrace"; يومئذ: يوم is a muḍāf to خزي, and يوم is itself a muḍāf, and the adverbial, which is إذ, is its muḍāf ilayhi. يوم is not given a fatḥa for its annexation to an indeclinable word, because the muḍāf is separated from the muḍāf ilayhi and annexation is not necessarily bound to it; so since annexation is not binding upon the muḍāf, indeclinability is not binding in it. It is also permissible to give يوم the fatḥa as indeclinable, because of its annexation to the indeclinable; among such cases is the words of Allah the Exalted: «Indeed it is the truth, just as you speak» (انه لحق مثل ما انكم تنطقون), where مثل is in the position of nominative and has been used as an adjective of an indefinite, but it is given fatḥa because of annexation to ما; more on this discussion will come. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ): inna and its ism; هو is a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; القوي العزيز is the khabar of inna, or of هو, and the clause is the khabar of inna. (وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دِيارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction according to the meaning; أخذ is a past verb from which the feminine tāʾ was dropped, either because the feminine, الصيحة, is figurative (not a true feminine), or because of the separation by the direct object; الذين is a direct object; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila; الصيحة is the agent; فأصبحوا is conjoined to أخذ, the wāw being the ism of أصبح and جاثمين its khabar; and في ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاثمين. (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها): كأن is the lightened form of the heavy (kaʾanna), and its ism is omitted, i.e. "as if they"; the clause لم يغنوا is its khabar; and فيها is attached to يغنوا. (أَلا إِنَّ ثَمُودَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ أَلا بُعْداً لِثَمُودَ): the i'rab of its like has already been given, letter for letter.

* Benefits:
The verbs that govern two objects (these are the verbs of the heart) have three rulings:
1- Iʿmāl (making them act): this is the basic rule for them, and it is putting two objects in the accusative.
2- Ilghāʾ (disregarding): it is the nullification of the action both in form and in position, because of the weakness of the governor through its being placed between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, or placed after them. An example of placing it in the middle: "Zayd, I think, is standing"; and of placing it after: "Zayd is standing, I think".
Manāzil ibn Rabīʿa al-Minqarī said:
أبالأراجيز يا ابن اللؤم توعدني ... وفي الأراجيز خلت اللؤم والخور
(Do you threaten me with rajaz verses, you son of vileness? And in rajaz verses, I thought, lie vileness and weakness.)
He placed خلت between the postponed mubtadaʾ, which is اللؤم, and the fronted khabar, which is في الأراجيز.
Abū Sayyida al-Dubayrī said:
وإن لنا شيخين لا ينفعاننا ... غنيين لا يجري علينا غناهما
(We have two elders who do not benefit us, rich, yet their wealth does not flow to us.)
هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما ... يسوداننا إن أيسرت غنماهما
(They are our two lords, so they claim; yet they lead us only if their sheep prosper.)
Disregarding a governor that is placed after is stronger than making it act, whereas for the governor placed in the middle it is the reverse: making it act is stronger than neglecting it.
3- Taʿlīq (suspension): it is the nullification of the action in form but not in position, because there follows it what has the right to the opening of the speech. That is: the lām of ibtidāʾ, as in «They certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter» (لقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق). من is a mubtadaʾ and a relative noun; the clause اشتراه is the ṣila of من, and its referent pronoun is the latent agent of اشتراه; ما is negative; له and في الآخرة are attached to the settling (istiqrār) which is the khabar of خلاق, and من is redundant; the clause ما له في الآخرة من خلاق is the khabar of من, the link between the two being the pronoun governed by the lām; and the clause of من and its khabar is in the position of accusative, the governor being suspended from it by the lām of ibtidāʾ, since it has the opening place, so no governor passes over it. [Translator's note: the source writes «من حلاق» in the verse quotation and «من خلاق» later; the verse is translated as «من خلاق».]
And the lām of oath, as in the words of Labīd:
ولقد علمت لتأتينّ منيتي ... إن المنايا لا تطيش سهامها
(I certainly knew that my death would come; indeed deaths' arrows do not miss.)
The lām in لتأتين is the lām of the response to an oath, and the oath with its response is in the position of accusative, the governor being suspended from it by the lām of oath.
And the negative mā, as in «You certainly know that these do not speak» (لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون): ما is negative, هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ and ينطقون its khabar, and the nominal sentence is in the position of accusative with علمت, the governor being suspended from it in form by the negative ما.
And the two negatives lā and in occurring in the response to an oath, either uttered or implied. An uttered oath, as in: "By Allah I know that Zayd is not in it, nor ʿAmr", and "By Allah I know that Zayd is not standing".
And interrogation, which has two forms:
(a) That an interrogative particle intervenes between the governor and the sentence after it, as in «And I do not know whether near or far is what you are promised» (وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون): قريب is a mubtadaʾ and أم بعيد is conjoined to it; ما is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and what is conjoined to it; the clause توعدون is the ṣila of the relative and its referent pronoun is omitted; and the sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of accusative with أدري, which is suspended by the hamza.
(b) That the sentence contains an interrogative noun that is a mainstay (ʿumda), as in «that We may know which of the two parties best computed the time they had stayed» (لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا): أي is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and أحصى is its khabar, which is a past verb (it is also said to be an elative from iḥṣāʾ, with the augments removed); the sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar is one from which نعلم is suspended, because no preceding word acts upon an interrogative. There is no difference among the mainstays between the mubtadaʾ, as above, and the khabar, as in "I know when the journey is"; or the muḍāf ilayhi, as in "I know whose father Zayd is"; or the khabar, as in "I know the morning of which day your journey is"; or an extra (faḍla), as in «Those who did wrong will know to what turn they will turn» (سيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون): أي منقلب is a mafʿūl muṭlaq accusative by ينقلبون, fronted from its place, the original being "ينقلبون أي انقلاب"; أي is not a direct object of يعلم, as one might imagine, because no preceding word acts upon an interrogative; and the clause ينقلبون is one from which the governor is suspended, so it is in the position of accusative.

Important note:
What is conjoined to the position of a sentence from which the governor is suspended is only a single word that contains the meaning of a sentence; so we say "I know that Zayd is standing, and other things of his affairs", but you do not say "I know that Zayd is standing and ʿAmr", because what these verbs seek is only the content of sentences; so if there is in the speech a single word which conveys the meaning of the sentence, it is correct to attach to it, otherwise not.
Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:
وما كنت أدري قبل عزة ما البكا ... ولا موجعات القلب حتى تولت
(Before ʿAzza I did not know what weeping was, nor the heart's aches, until she turned away.)
He conjoined موجعات in the accusative, with the kasra as its sign, to the position of ما البكا, from which the action of أدري was suspended. The discussions of ilghāʾ and taʿlīq are too narrow for these benefits to encompass, so what we have mentioned is enough; whoever wishes more should consult the longer works.

dervis-irab:96-108.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَقْدُمُ): One says قدمت القوم أقدمهم قدما when you walk ahead of them and they follow you. Al-Azharī said: qadama yaqdumu, taqaddama, qaddama, aqdama and istaqdama have the same meaning.
(الْوِرْدُ): the coming to water that one comes to, and the camels that come to it; the plural is awrād. Al-īrād is making the coming to water obligatory, or what takes its place. Labīd said:
فوردنا قبل فراط القطا ... إن من وردي تغليس النهل
(We came to water before the sandgrouse flocks went ahead; indeed part of my watering is coming at the darkness before dawn for the first drink.) The basis of wurūd is to look over the point of entry, not entering. Zuhayr said:
فلما وردن الماء زرقا جمامه ... وضعن عصي الحاضر المتوسم
(When they came to the water, its pools blue, they laid down the staffs of the one who settles and takes note of signs.)
(الرِّفْدُ): help in a matter. One says rafadahu yarfiduhu rafdan and rifdan, with a fatḥa or a kasra on the rāʾ. Al-Zajjāj said: anything you make a help to something, and by which you prop something up, you have "raffadtahu" with it. One says ʿamadtu to the wall, and asnadtuhu, arfadtuhu and rafadtuhu, all with one meaning. One says rafadahu and arfadahu when he gave him; the noun is al-rifd, because a gift is a help to the one given to.
(الحصيد): in the sense of al-maḥṣūd (the reaped). Al-ḥaṣd is cutting crops from the root. This is the season of al-ḥaṣād, with a fatḥa or a kasra on the ḥāʾ. One says ḥaṣadahum bi-l-sayf when he killed them.
(تَتْبِيبٍ): from tabbat yaduhu, i.e. it lost and perished. Jarīr said:
عرابة من بقية قوم لوط ... ألا تبا لما فعلوه تبا
(ʿArāba is of the remnant of the people of Lūṭ; alas, ruin, ruin to what they did.)
(الزفير والشهيق): al-zafīr is the repeating of the breath until the ribs open from it, and al-shahīq is the drawing of the breath back into the chest. Ibn Fāris said: al-zafīr is the opposite of al-shahīq, because al-shahīq is drawing the breath back and al-zafīr is expelling the breath out of intense grief; it is taken from al-zafr, which is carrying a load on the back because of its heaviness. It is also said that al-shahīq is the prolonged breath, taken from their saying jabal shāhiq, i.e. high. Al-Layth said: al-zafīr is when a man fills his chest with breath while in intense distress, and al-shahīq is when that breath goes out. It is close to their saying tanaffasa l-ṣuʿadāʾ (he sighed deeply). Abū l-ʿĀliya and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: al-zafīr is in the throat and al-shahīq is in the chest. It is also said that al-zafīr belongs to the donkey and al-shahīq to the mule. Al-Thaʿālibī said in Tartīb al-Aṣwāt:
When the afflicted or sick person lets out a soft sound, it is al-ranīn; when he hides it, it is al-hanīn; when he shows it and it comes out faint, it is al-khanīn; when he exhales with it and the groaning is ugly, it is al-zafīr; when he draws out the breath and then throws it out, it is al-shahīq; and when his breath rattles in his chest as it goes out, it is al-ḥashraja.
(مَجْذُوذٍ): cut off. Al-jadhdh is cutting; one says jadhdahu yajudhdhuhu, and its pattern is radda, as in al-Mukhtār; and "Allah cut off their rear". Al-Nābigha said:
تجذ السلوقي المضاعف نسجه ... وتوقد بالصّفّاح نار الحباحب
(She cuts through the Salūqī mail, its weave doubled, and with the flat stones she kindles the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib.)

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): This is the seventh and last story in this sūra. It was preceded by the story of Nūḥ, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Ibrāhīm, Lūṭ and Shuʿayb, in this order, and this is the story of Mūsā. بآياتنا is ḥāl, i.e. "being accompanied by Our nine signs", to which reference has already been made; وسلطان is conjoined to آياتنا; and مبين is naʿt. (إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ فَاتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَما أَمْرُ فِرْعَوْنَ بِرَشِيدٍ): إلى فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا; وملئه is conjoined to فرعون; فاتبعوا is conjoined to أرسلنا and the wāw is the fāʿil; أمر فرعون is mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial; mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; أمر is its noun; and برشيد is its khabar, with the bāʾ redundant; a parallel has already been given. (يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ وَبِئْسَ الْوِرْدُ الْمَوْرُودُ): The clause يقدم قومه is resumptive; the fāʾ is a conjunction; أوردهم النار is a verb with a latent fāʿil, the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and النار is the second mafʿūl bihi. It came in the past form, although the flow of the speech requires the imperfect, in order to show the scene as if it were a matter decided and finished with. Bi'sa is a past, inflexible verb for expressing censure; الورد is the fāʿil; المورود is naʿt; and the one specified for censure is omitted, i.e. "their coming". (وَأُتْبِعُوا فِي هذِهِ لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ بِئْسَ الرِّفْدُ الْمَرْفُودُ): اتبعوا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; في هذه is attached to اتبعوا, and the demonstrative refers to the life of this world; ويوم القيامة is conjoined to the position of في هذه; the meaning is that a curse was attached to them in this world and in the next. The i'rab of بئس الرفد المرفود has already been given. (ذلِكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْقُرى نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْها قائِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ): ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; من أنباء القرى is its first khabar; the clause نقصه is its second khabar; عليك is attached to نقصه; منها is a fronted khabar; قائم is the mubtadaʾ; and حصيد is conjoined to قائم. The sentence is resumptive, i.e. some of them have had their traces erased and their marks wiped out, and some remain standing visibly. The resumption is explanatory, as if it were the answer to a questioner asking about them. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: منها قائم is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of ḥāl from the hāʾ in نقصه, and حصيد is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "and among them is a reaped one". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that the clause be circumstantial; he said: "The ḥāl is more effective in frightening and in setting an example for those present." (وَما ظَلَمْناهُمْ وَلكِنْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; mā is negative; ظلمناهم is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; lākin is inoperative, for rectification; ظلموا أنفسهم is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. (فَما أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ آلِهَتُهُمُ الَّتِي يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; mā is negative; أغنت is a past verb; عنهم is attached to أغنت; آلهتهم is the fāʿil; التي is naʿt; the clause يدعون is the ṣila; من دون الله is ḥāl; min is redundant; and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. (لَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَما زادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ): Lammā is a ẓarf of time, attached to أغنت, or it is a connective; جاء أمر ربك is a verb and a fāʿil. وما زادوهم is conjoined to ما أغنت; the wāw of rational beings is used for the gods because they placed them in their position; زادوهم is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; and غير تتبيب is a second mafʿūl bihi. (وَكَذلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذا أَخَذَ الْقُرى وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ)
The kāf is in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ, and أخذ ربك is the khabar. In idhā akhadha l-qurā, idhā is a ẓarf of the future, and the clause أخذ القرى is in the genitive position through the ẓarf's annexation to it. The wāw is circumstantial; هي is a mubtadaʾ; ظالمة is the khabar; and the sentence is accusative as ḥāl. It is worth pointing out that the matter here is one of mutual claim (tanāzuʿ): the maṣdar and akhadha both claim al-qurā, so the verb was given the operation and the pronoun was omitted from the maṣdar; and the apodosis of idhā, which is what governs it, is omitted, the implied form being "then nothing of His seizing avails them". (إِنَّ أَخْذَهُ أَلِيمٌ شَدِيدٌ): Inna and its noun and its two khabars.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِمَنْ خافَ عَذابَ الْآخِرَةِ): Inna is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; آية is its delayed noun; لمن is naʿt of آية; and the clause خاف عذاب الآخرة is the ṣila. (ذلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ وَذلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ): ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; يوم is the khabar; مجموع is naʿt; له is attached to مجموع; الناس is the nāʾib fāʿil; and ذلك يوم مشهود is conjoined to what preceded it. A preposition and its genitive noun must be implied, i.e. "witnessed in it". The secret of that will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَما نُؤَخِّرُهُ إِلَّا لِأَجَلٍ مَعْدُودٍ): The wāw is resumptive; mā is negative; نؤخره is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; illā is a particle of restriction; لأجل is attached to نؤخره; and معدود is naʿt. (يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ): The statements of the parsers about this verse have been greatly confused, and they have wandered into labyrinths in which the seeker of truth and unforced ease is lost. We shall choose the answers that cannot be avoided, passing over lengthy discussion, and we say: the ẓarf is attached to his saying لا تكلم, i.e. "no soul will speak on that very day"; the clause يأتي is annexed to the ẓarf; and the fāʿil of يأتي is a pronoun referring to that day mentioned before, not the pronoun of the "day" that is annexed to يأتي. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that the fāʿil of يأتي is Allah, mighty and exalted, because the pronoun in بإذنه refers to Him. That is a plausible view, but the first is closer to the flow of the speech. Lā is negative; تكلم is an imperfect verb whose original form is تتكلم, with one of its two tāʾs dropped; نفس is the fāʿil of تكلم; illā is a particle of restriction; and بإذنه is ḥāl. (فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ): The fāʾ is for ramification; منهم is a fronted khabar; شقي is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and سعيد is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "and among them is a happy one". (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ): The fāʾ is also for ramification; ammā is a particle of condition and detailing; الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause شقوا is the ṣila; the fāʾ is the connective; and في النار is the khabar of الذين. (لَهُمْ فِيها زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ): لهم is a fronted khabar; فيها is ḥāl, because it was an adjective of زفير; زفير is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and شهيق is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is also omitted. (خالِدِينَ فِيها ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ): خالدين is ḥāl from الذين شقوا; فيها is attached to خالدين; and in ما دامت السموات, mā is a temporal maṣdar, and dāmat here is complete (tāmma) since it means "remained"; السموات is the fāʿil of دامت; and الأرض is conjoined. (إِلَّا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ): Illā is a particle of exception; mā is the excepted; the discussion of this problematic exception will come in the section on Benefits; and the clause شاء ربك is the ṣila. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ): Inna and its noun and khabar; لما is attached to فعال; and the clause يريد is the ṣila. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ خالِدِينَ فِيها ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ): Its i'rab was given just above.
Ibn Masʿūd, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read سُعِدوا with a ḍamma on the sīn, and the rest of the Seven and the majority read it with a fatḥa. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān used to marvel at al-Kisāʾī's reading سُعِدوا despite his knowledge of Arabic, but there is no cause for marvel at that, since it is a reading transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd and those we have mentioned with him. Al-Kisāʾī argued from their saying masʿūd; it was said that there is no proof in it, because one says "a place masʿūd fīhi", then fīhi was dropped and it was used as a name. Al-Thaʿlabī said: "saʿida and asʿada have one meaning." In al-Asās: "saʿidtu bihi and suʿidtu, and he is saʿīd and masʿūd." In al-Qāmūs: "He has saʿida, like ʿalima and ʿunia, so he is saʿīd and masʿūd, and one does not say musʿad." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "One says saʿida l-rajul as one says ḥasuna", and it was said that saʿadahu is an abandoned dialect; a group weakened the reading of the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], and it is the reading of Ḥafṣ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: saʿida fulān yasʿadu, of the pattern taʿiba, in religion or worldly affairs, saʿdan; it is named from the maṣdar, the agent is saʿīd and the plural is suʿadāʾ. In one dialect it is made transitive by the vowel, so one says saʿadahu Allāh yasʿaduhu, with two fatḥas, and he is masʿūd. Among the Seven, this dialect was read in his saying وأما الذين سعدوا in the passive; most commonly it is made transitive by the hamza, so one says asʿadahu Allāh; and suʿida with a ḍamma is the opposite of shaqiya.
(عَطاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ): عطاء is accusative as a maṣdar confirming the sense of the preceding sentence, because his saying ففي الجنة خالدين فيها requires giving and bestowing favour; and غير مجذوذ is naʿt of عطاء.

* Rhetoric:
These verses embrace varied arts of rhetoric and a group of benefits:
1- The first is the use of the passive participle in place of its verb in the saying of the Exalted:
«ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود». The secret of preferring the passive participle is to describe the day with the sense of gathering, settled fixity and the permanence of that fixity in it, and that it is a day appointed to be a fixed rendezvous, with no escape from it and no allowance for changing it, for all people alike. Had the verb been used, it would not have fallen in that place, and it would have suggested renewal and change. Its like is the saying of the one threatening: "Your property is plundered (lamanhūb) and your people are ravaged (maḥrūb)", in which there is a fixity and permanence of description that the verb does not have, and breadth in the ẓarf.
2-3 The second and third are combination with separation (al-jamʿ maʿa l-tafrīq): the combination is in his saying «لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه» and the separation is in his saying «فمنهم شقي وسعيد».
4- Division (al-taqsīm) in his saying «فأما الذين شقوا» to the end of the verse. Among the examples of combination with separation in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī:
ولما التقينا والنقا موعد لنا ... تعجّب رائي الدّر منا ولاقطه
فمن لؤلؤ تجلوه عند ابتسامها ... ومن لؤلؤ عند الحديث تساقطه
(When we met, the sand dune being our rendezvous, the one who saw the pearls and the one who gathered them marvelled at us; some are pearls she reveals when she smiles, and some are pearls that fall when she speaks.)
As for division, Arabic poetry brims with it. Abū Nuwās said, dividing time into today, yesterday and tomorrow:
أمر غد أنت منه في لبس ... وأمس قد فات فاله عن أمس
وانما الشأن شأن يومك ذا ... فباكر الشمس بابنة الشمس
(Tomorrow's affair, about which you are in confusion; and yesterday has passed, so be distracted from yesterday; the real concern is the concern of this day of yours, so meet the sun early with the daughter of the sun [wine].)
They were highly inventive in it, and Abū l-Ṭayyib applied it to the states of the thing to be divided, adding to each of those states what suits it. He said:
سأطلب حقي بالقنا ومشايخ ... كأنهم من طول ما التثموا مرد
ثقال إذا لاقوا خفاف إذا دعوا ... كثير إذا شدّوا قليل إذا عدوا
(I shall seek my right with lances and with elders who, from how long they have worn the face veil, seem beardless youths; heavy when they meet, light when called; many when they charge, few when counted.)
And he has also:
الدهر معتذر والسيف منتظر ... وأرضهم لك مصطاف ومرتبع
للسبي ما نكحوا والقتل ما ولدوا ... والنهب ما جمعوا والنار ما زرعوا
(Time apologizes and the sword waits, and their land is for you a summer place and a spring pasture; for captivity is what they married, for killing what they begot, for plunder what they gathered, and for fire what they sowed.)
And in love poetry:
وأغيد يهوى نفسه كلّ عاقل ... ظريف ويهوى جسمه كل فاسق
سهاد لأجفان وشمس لناظر ... وسقم لأبدان ومسك لناشق
(A tender-necked beauty whom every refined, intelligent man loves for his soul, and every libertine loves for his body; wakefulness to the eyelids, a sun to the beholder, sickness to bodies and musk to the one who smells.)
How lovely is the saying of ʿUmar ibn al-Fāriḍ:
يقولون لي: صفها فأنت بوصفها ... خبير أجل عندي بأوصافها علم
صفاء ولا ماء ولطف ولا هوا ... ونور ولا نار وروح ولا جسم
(They say to me: "Describe her, for you are expert in describing her." Yes, I have knowledge of her attributes: purity but not water, subtlety but not air, light but not fire, spirit but not body.)

* Benefits:
The exception present in the saying of the Exalted «إلا ما شاء ربك» was discussed in Sūrat al-Anʿām, so renew your acquaintance with it. We favoured there the view that al-Zajjāj took, and we add to it here that al-Farrāʾ took the view that al-Zajjāj took, and said something delicate about it, which we relay to be added to what preceded. He said: "It is an exception regarding the increase of punishment for the people of the Fire and the increase of bliss for the people of Paradise; the implied meaning is 'except what your Lord wills of increase beyond this measure', as a man says to another, 'I am owed a thousand dinars by you, except the two thousand that I lent you at such and such a time.' The two thousand are an addition to the thousand without doubt, because the larger is not excepted from the smaller." I saw words to this effect from ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā, known as al-Rummānī. The sum of what has preceded is that illā in meaning is a conjunction particle, and the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), as if it were said: "abiding in it as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and in addition to this period", so illā is as if it meant wāw. Al-Farrāʾ recited as evidence for that:
وأرى لها دارا بأغدر السيدان لم يدرس لها رسم
إلا رمادا هامدا رفعت ... عنه الرياح خوالد سحم
(And I see for her a dwelling at the pools of al-Sīdān whose traces have not been effaced, except dead ash from which the winds have lifted the lasting, black [hearthstones].)
This view, which we have chosen and which al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ took, is the thirteenth; there are twelve differing views.
It would take us long to relay these views, so whoever wishes may consult the major commentaries to see how understandings differ. It pleases us to relay here an opinion that needs interpretation, belonging to the philosopher of the Sufis, Muḥyī al-Dīn Ibn ʿArabī. He said: they are punished in it for a time, then it turns upon them and a fiery nature remains for them, in which they take pleasure because of its agreement with their nature, for praise is for the truth of the promise, not for the truth of the threat. And he said elsewhere: when the people of the Fire enter it, they remain fearful, expecting to be taken out of it; but when its doors are closed upon them they are reassured, because it was created in accordance with their natures.
In the modern age, Badawī al-Jabal has a brilliant poem in which he says, describing the people of the Fire:
لا يألمون ولا تشكو جسومهم ... من اللظى فهي نيران بنيران
(They feel no pain and their bodies do not complain of the flame, for it is fires in fires.)
Ibn al-Qayyim commented on this saying: "This is at one extreme, and the Muʿtazila, who say that Allah is obliged to punish whoever He threatened with punishment, are at the other extreme; for them, whoever enters the Fire never escapes it at all." Al-Zamakhsharī went on at length in condemning the Sunnis in this regard, which would take long to discuss; we have relayed these glimpses only for information.

dervis-irab:109-112.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مِرْيَةٍ): al-miryā, with a kasra or a ḍamma on the mīm, is doubt despite the appearance of evidence for suspicion. It is taken from maral ḍarʿ al-nāqa, "he milked the she-camel's udder" so that it would yield after its yielding had stopped. Imtarā fī l-shayʾ means he doubted; istamrā l-laban and the like means he drew it out and made it flow.

* I'rab:
(فَلا تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِمَّا يَعْبُدُ هؤُلاءِ): The fāʾ is resumptive. The sentence is brought to indicate the effect the preceding stories produced in his soul ﷺ, and that the devotion of the disbelievers of Quraysh to worshipping their idols is not among the causes that discourage his resolve. Lā is prohibitive; تك is an imperfect verb, jussive by lā, its sign of jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn, which was dropped for lightness (the properties of kāna have been mentioned before); its noun is a latent pronoun, implied "you"; في مرية is its khabar; مما is naʿt; the clause يعبد is the ṣila; and هؤلاء is the fāʿil. It is permissible that mā be a maṣdar. (ما يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ): Mā is negative; يعبدون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; illā is a particle of restriction; the kāf is naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; mā may be relative or maṣdar; and من قبل is attached to an omitted element as ḥāl. (وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنْقُوصٍ): The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; موفوهم is the khabar of inna; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; نصيبهم is mafʿūl bihi; and غير منقوص is a ḥāl clarifying the share that is paid in full. It is also said that it is rather a confirming ḥāl, because paying in full necessarily entails no shortfall in what is paid, whether it is complete or deficient: your saying "I paid him half of his right" entails that there is no shortfall, so what is the ground for its being accusative as a ḥāl from it? The more tenable view is that "paying in full" is used in the sense of "giving", and whoever says "I gave so-and-so his due" would be worthy of confirming it with the words "without being diminished".
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ فَاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ): The wāw is resumptive; the lām prepares for the oath; qad is a particle of certainty; آتينا موسى الكتاب is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. In فاختلف, the fāʾ is a conjunction and اختلف is a passive past verb, and فيه fills the place of the nāʾib fāʿil; the meaning of fī is containment, i.e. "concerning it", and it is also said to be causal. (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; lawlā is a particle indicating the prevention of one thing by the existence of another; كلمة is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause سبقت is naʿt; من ربك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سبقت; the lām is the apodosis of law; قضي بينهم is a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil latent, and the ẓarf is attached to it, i.e. "and the matter would have been decided between them". (وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مُرِيبٍ): The wāw is circumstantial; inna and its noun; في شك is its khabar; منه is naʿt of شك; and مريب is a second naʿt.
(وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ رَبُّكَ أَعْمالَهُمْ): This verse is very problematic, and the difficulty increases in our reading, which is the doubling of inn and the heavy lammā. The early parsers admitted their inability. Al-Samīn said, in these words: "This noble verse is among those that people have discussed, in ancient and modern times, and most of them found it difficult to summarize, as to reading and analysis; Allah the Exalted has made that easy, so I have mentioned their statements and which of them is preferable", then he wandered into remote labyrinths in which the student is lost. As is our custom we shall pass over those diverging aspects and conflicting paths and content ourselves with our reading, which is the reading of Ḥafṣ, Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza. We say: inna and its noun. As for lammā, they mentioned four aspects for it; the easiest, and the furthest from forced reading, is what al-Zajjāj chose: that it means illā, as in their saying "I ask you lammā you did", meaning illā. This is an easy aspect by which every difficulty disappears, were it not for its conflict with what al-Farrāʾ said: "This is not permitted except in wishing, as al-Khalīl said, or after negation, like His saying «إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ»." Yet, with what is in it, it is easier than the other three aspects. They are that it be in the sense of la-min-mā, with the three mīms dropped, which al-Farrāʾ chose, reciting:
وإني لمما أصدر الأمر وجهه ... إذا هو أعيا بالسبيل مصادره
(I am among those who direct a matter toward its proper course when its outlets have failed to find the way.)
The second is that it be lightened and doubled for emphasis, which is al-Māzinī's choice; but this is rejected, because lightening of a doubled particle is permissible only in necessity, whereas doubling a lightened one is not permitted at all. The fourth aspect is that it is a maṣdar of lamma, from lamamtu l-shayʾ when you gathered it, except that it was built as indeclinable and not made diptote-inflected, as if he had said "and every one together will surely be paid in full"; and in this there is what there is, and Allah knows best. As for ليوفينهم: the lām is the answer to an implied oath; يوفينهم is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the hāʾ is its object; ربك is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna; and أعمالهم is a second mafʿūl bihi. (إِنَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): Inna and its noun; بما يعملون is attached to خبير; and خبير is the khabar of inna. (فَاسْتَقِمْ كَما أُمِرْتَ وَمَنْ تابَ مَعَكَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); استقم is an imperative verb; the kāf is naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "so stand firm with a standing firm like the standing firm you were commanded, on the path of truth, not deviating from it". As for ومن: the wāw is a conjunction and man is a relative conjoined to the pronoun in استقم; conjunction to it without emphasis by a detached pronoun is permitted because the intervening element stands in its place; معك is a ẓarf attached to an omitted element as the ṣila of the relative, and it may be a mafʿūl maʿahu with the wāw meaning accompaniment. (وَلا تَطْغَوْا إِنَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): Lā is prohibitive; تطغوا is an imperfect verb jussive by lā and the wāw is the fāʿil; inna and its noun; بما تعملون and its khabar; its like has already been given.

* Rhetoric:
Concision (al-ījāz) in the saying of the Exalted «فاستقم». That is because uprightness (istiqāma) is continuing in one direction and not swerving right or left. It is well known that the straight line is the shortest distance between two points, so the slightest deviation takes it out of its straightness. Therefore the word istiqāma has gathered all noble character traits, the fine rulings of the basic and derived kinds, and the perfections sought by the knowers and the near ones. Slackening from it is dangerous, and avoiding slackening is hard. For that reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, in a ḥadīth narrated by Ibn ʿAbbās, when his Companions said to him, "Grey hair has hastened upon you": «شيبتني هود والواقعة وأخواتهما».

* Benefits:
What Abū Ḥayyān says:
Abū Ḥayyān said: "As for the second reading, the doubling of inna and its operating on kull is clear. As for the doubling of lammā, al-Mubarrad said: 'This is a solecism (laḥn); the Arabs do not say inna Zaydan lammā khārij.' This is audacity on the part of al-Mubarrad, as is his habit. How can a mutawātir reading be a solecism? The construction of the verse is not like the construction of the example he cited, inna Zaydan lammā khārij; that example is a solecism, but in the verse it is not. Had he been silent and said what al-Kisāʾī said — 'I do not know the ground of this reading' — he would have been guided aright. As for the grammarians other than these two, they differed over its analysis."
Then Abū Ḥayyān cited a flood of analyses and rejected them all, among them the aspect we chose, and said at the end:
"These are all very weak analyses, from which the Qur'an is to be kept clear. There appeared to me an aspect running on the rules of Arabic, namely that this lammā is the jussive lammā whose jussive verb has been omitted because the meaning indicates it, as they omitted it in their saying:
قاربت المدينة ولما يريدون ولما أدخلها
(I drew near the city, and they [had] not yet wanted [it], and I had not yet entered it.)
and likewise here: the implied meaning is 'and every one, nothing has yet been deducted from the recompense of his deeds'. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted «ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم»: when He reported that no portion of the recompense of their deeds would be deducted, He confirmed it with the oath, so He said, «ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم». I had thought that I had been first to this sound analysis, free of forced reading, and I mentioned it to someone who reads with me, who said: 'Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib has mentioned it.' Because I had left off looking into this man's words, I had not come across it. Then I saw in the book al-Taḥrīr the relaying of this analysis from Ibn al-Ḥājib. He said: 'This lammā is the jussive one, its verb omitted because of the indication of it, since the omission of its verb is established in their saying "I went out, and had not yet travelled" and the like, and it is sound and eloquent. The implied meaning is "had not yet been left", on account of what preceded as an indication of it, namely the detailing of the two groups in His saying "among them is a wretched one and a happy one"; then He mentioned the wretched and the happy and their recompense, then clarified that by His saying "your Lord will surely pay them in full for their deeds".' He said: 'I know of no aspect more similar than this, though souls find it remote on the ground that nothing like it occurred in the Qur'an.'"

dervis-irab:69-76.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العجل): the offspring of the cow; it is also called al-ḥasīl and al-khabash in the dialect of the people of al-Sarāt. Its plural is ʿujūl, ʿijala, ʿijāl and ʿajājīl. It is said that it is so named because of the hastening (taʿjīl) of its affair, by the nearness of its birth.
(حَنِيذٍ): what is roasted on heated stones in a pit in the ground, which is the practice of the desert dwellers. It was fat, with its grease dripping from it, and most of Ibrāhīm's wealth was cattle. In al-Mukhtār: "ḥanadha al-shāh" means he roasted it and put heated stones over it so that it would be cooked, so it is ḥanīdh; its verbal pattern is like ḍaraba.
(نَكِرَهُمْ): in al-Mukhtār: "nakirahu" (with kasra), "nukran" (with ḍamma on the nūn), and "ankarahu" are all of one meaning. The wording of al-Asās is: "He disowned the thing (ankara), disliked it (nakira) and found it strange (istankara). It is said that nakira is stronger than ankara; and it is said: nakira is with the heart and ankara with the eye. Al-Aʿshā said:
وأنكرتني وما كان الذي نكرت ... من الحوادث إلا الشيب والصلعا
(She did not recognize me, and all that she disowned of the calamities was grey hair and baldness.)
Among them are al-ʿurf and al-nukr, al-maʿrūf and al-munkar; 'So-and-so was reviled and had no denial (nakīr) in him'; 'they commit abominations (munkarāt) and atrocities (manākīr)'; and 'he is among the atrocities of the people of Lūṭ.'"
(أَوْجَسَ): al-ījās is sensing and the speech of the soul; its origin is from entering, as if fear entered him; al-wajīs is what befalls the soul, or fright; "wajasa fī nafsihi kadhā" means such-and-such crossed his mind, wajasa yajisu, with verbal nouns wajsan, wujūsan and wajīsan.
(بَعْلِي): al-baʿl is the one who is above others. Since a woman's husband is above her and takes charge of her affairs, he is called baʿl. They also call a palm tree that does without river and spring water, being satisfied by rain, baʿl, because it stands on its own in its not needing the trouble of irrigation. The plural of baʿl is buʿūl, biʿāl and buʿūla. Al-baʿl is also the lord and the master; they say "man baʿlu hādhihi al-nāqa" meaning "who is the owner of this she-camel?" And in this sense the Canaanites and others among the idol-worshippers used it to indicate the greatest of their gods.
(أَوَّاهٌ): its meanings appeared earlier in Sūrat al-Tawba.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا إِبْراهِيمَ بِالْبُشْرى): Then Allah, glorified be He, began the fourth story of the stories of the sūra, namely the story of Ibrāhīm, as an introduction to the story of Lūṭ and not for itself; for this reason the manner of the story differs from the preceding ones, and He did not say "and We sent". The lām is the response to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; جاءت رسلنا: a verb and an agent; إبراهيم is a direct object; and بالبشرى is attached to جاءت.
(قالُوا سَلاماً قالَ سَلامٌ): قالوا: a verb and an agent; سلاما is a maṣdar governed by an omitted verb, as already mentioned, i.e. "we greet you with a greeting"; قال is a past verb; and سلام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon you"; the meaning of supplication permitted the mubtadaʾ to be indefinite, and this is preferable to making it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "my saying is 'peace'"; the justifications for beginning with an indefinite will come in the section on Benefits. (فَما لَبِثَ أَنْ جاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; as for ما in ما لبث, it may be negative, with لبث a past verb whose agent is أن and what is in its scope, i.e. "his bringing"; or the agent is latent, its implied form being "Ibrāhīm", and أن and what is in its scope is its khabar, the implied form being "so his delay" or "the one he delayed was the measure of his bringing".
(فَلَمَّا رَأى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً): the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, the implied form being "so he brought it near to them, but they did not stretch out their hands, so he said: Will you not eat? So when he saw their hands"; the seeing here is by the eye; أيديهم is a direct object; the clause لا تصل إليه is a ḥāl clause; the clause نكرهم has no grammatical position because it is the response of لما; وأوجس منهم is conjoined to نكرهم; خيفة is a direct object; and منهم is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of خيفة. (قالُوا لا تَخَفْ إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنا إِلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ): لا تخف: لا is prohibitive and تخف is jussive by it; inna and its ism; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar, نا being the deputy agent; and إلى قوم لوط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا. (وَامْرَأَتُهُ قائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها بِإِسْحاقَ وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ): وامرأته: the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; امرأته is a mubtadaʾ and قائمة a khabar; فضحكت is a past verb whose agent is "she"; فبشرناها is also a conjunction, a verb, an agent and a direct object; بإسحاق is attached to بشرناها; ومن وراء إسحاق is a fronted khabar and يعقوب a postponed mubtadaʾ. (قالَتْ: يا وَيْلَتى أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا عَجُوزٌ): يا ويلتا is an expression said in wonder at a marvellous matter that breaks custom, whether good or evil; it is the one addressed, annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker which has turned into alif, likewise in "yā lahfā" and "yā ʿajabā"; it is also said that it is the alif of lamentation (nudba), on which one stops with the hāʾ of pause, and the discussion of it will come in its place. أألد: the interrogative is meant as wonder; the wāw is circumstantial; أنا is a mubtadaʾ and عجوز a khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in أألد. (وَهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً إِنَّ هذا لَشَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and بعلي a khabar; شيخا is a ḥāl, the governor in it being the verbal meaning in the demonstrative. Al-Zajjāj said: the accusative of the ḥāl here is among the subtleties of grammar. That is, when you say "this is Zayd standing, praying": if you intend to inform someone who does not know Zayd that he is Zayd, it is not permissible to say "this is Zayd standing", because he would be "Zayd" only so long as he is standing, and once he leaves standing he is not Zayd. You say "this is Zayd standing" only to someone who knows Zayd, so alerting acts on the ḥāl, the meaning being "Attend to Zayd while he is standing", or "I point out Zayd to you while he is standing".
Then inna and its ism; the shifted lām; شيء is its khabar and عجيب an adjective. (قالُوا: أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ): the hamza is for interrogation, the intent being prohibition, i.e. "do not be astonished"; they did not rebuke her, because her astonishment was not denial but only bewilderment at what breaks custom; تعجبين is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the yāʾ being the agent; and من أمر الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعجبين. (رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ): رحمة الله is a mubtadaʾ; وبركاته is conjoined to رحمة; عليكم is the khabar of رحمة; أهل البيت is accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), intended as praise; it may also be a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted, i.e. "O people of the house"; and inna with its ism and two khabars.
There is a difference between the accusative of praise and the accusative of ikhtiṣāṣ, and for this reason Sībawayh made them two separate chapters: the accusative of praise is a word that by its very placing includes praise, just as the accusative of blame includes blame by its placing; while the accusative of ikhtiṣāṣ occurs only for praise or blame but its wording by its placing includes neither praise nor blame, as in the line «بنا تميما يكشف الضباب» ("Through us, Tamīm, the fog is lifted") and the line «ولا الحجاج عيني نبت ماء» ("...nor al-Ḥajjāj, my eye..."). [Translator's note: the second verse fragment is given as in the source, incomplete.] (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْراهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ وَجاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرى): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or connective; ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع: a verb and an agent; وجاءته البشرى is conjoined to ذهب; and the response of لما is omitted, its implied form being "he turned" or "he grasped, in order to dispute with them".
(يُجادِلُنا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ): the clause يجادلنا is circumstantial or resumptive, and في قوم لوط is attached to يجادلنا. (إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ): inna and its ism; the shifted lām; حليم, أواه and منيب are three khabars. (يا إِبْراهِيمُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هذا): the sentence is the reported speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "the angels said"; أعرض is an imperative verb; عن هذا is attached to it, the pointing being to the dispute. (إِنَّهُ قَدْ جاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَإِنَّهُمْ آتِيهِمْ عَذابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ): inna and its ism; the clause قد جاء أمر ربك is the khabar; وإنهم: inna and its ism; آتيهم is its khabar; عذاب is the agent of آتيهم; غير is an adjective and مردود a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
Representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in His words: «When he saw that their hands did not reach it» (فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه): the non-reaching is made a metaphor for their refraining from eating; the meaning is "they do not stretch out their hands to eat it", for he does not intend to deny a reaching that arises from stretching out.

* Benefits:
The justifications for beginning with an indefinite:
What is obligatory in the mubtadaʾ is that it be definite, and beginning with an indefinite is permitted if it conveys a benefit, in several places, the most important of which are:
1- By verbal annexation, as in «Five prayers Allah has prescribed» (خمس صلوات كتبهن الله); the annexation may also be in meaning, as in «Say: each acts according to his manner» (قل كلّ يعمل على شاكلته), i.e. "each one".
2- By an adjective, in wording, as in «A believing slave is better than a polytheist» (لعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك); or in implication, as in "An (affair) has come from your Lord", i.e. "a great one"; or in meaning, when the indefinite is a diminutive, as in "rujayl (a little man) is with us", i.e. "a despicable man".
3- By its khabar being an adverbial, or a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted before it, as in «and above every possessor of knowledge is a knower» (وفوق كل ذي علم عليم) and «for every term is a decree» (ولكل أجل كتاب).
4- By its occurring after a negation, an interrogative, lawlā, or the idhā of surprise, as in: "No one is with us"; and as in «Is there a god with Allah?» (أإله مع الله); and the verse of the poet:
لولا اصطبار الأودى كل ذي مقة ... لما استقلّت مطاياهنّ للظّعن
(Were it not for the patience of every loving al-Awdī, their mounts would not have risen for departure.)
and as in: "I went out and behold a lion lying in wait".
5- By its being a governor, as in: "Giving a piastre for the sake of knowledge raises the nation."
6- By its being vague, like the conditional and interrogative nouns, the exclamatory mā, and the declarative kam.
7- By its conveying supplication for good or evil: the first as in «Peace be upon you» (سلام عليكم), and the second as in «Woe to the defrauders» (ويل للمطففين).
8- By its being a substitute for a qualified noun, as in: "A knowledgeable one is better than an ignorant one."
9- By its occurring at the head of a circumstantial clause, as in:
سرينا ونجم قد أضاء فمذ بدا ... محياك أخفى ضوءه كلّ شارق
(We travelled while a star was shining; then, when your face appeared, every rising one hid its light.)
10- By its being intended for classification, i.e. detailing and dividing, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فأقبلت زحفا على الركبتين ... فثوب نسيت وثوب أجر
(I approached, crawling upon my two knees; one garment I forgot, another I drag.)
11- By its being conjoined to a definite, or a definite being conjoined to it, as in: "Khālid and a man are learning grammar", or "a man and Khālid are learning grammar".
12- By its being conjoined to a qualified indefinite, as in «A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury» (قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى).
13- By its being intended for the reality of the genus and not a single individual of it, as in: "A date is better than a locust."
14- By its occurring as an answer, as in: "A man", in answer to one who said: "Who is with you?"

dervis-irab:113-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَرْكَنُوا): al-rukūn to a thing is to be at rest in it through love for it, and to listen attentively to it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "I inclined to Zayd (rakantu ilā Zayd)" means I relied on him. It has several dialects. One is of the pattern taʿiba, on which the saying of the Exalted «ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا» rests; and rakana rukūnan of the pattern qaʿada — al-Azharī said it is not the eloquent form. The third is rakana yarkanu with two fatḥas, which is not original but arises from the interpenetration of two dialects, because the pattern faʿila yafʿalu has a guttural as its ʿayn or lām." Al-Rāghib said: "The correct view is that one says rakana yarkanu with a fatḥa in both, and rakina yarkanu with a kasra in the past and a fatḥa in the imperfect, and with a fatḥa in the past and a ḍamma in the imperfect." It is gathered from al-Qāmūs and its commentary and other dictionaries that it is of the pattern dakhala and of the pattern taʿiba. As for its intransitive sense, its pattern is rakuna with a ḍamma on the kāf, meaning he was steady and dignified.
(زُلَفاً): with a ḍamma on the zāy and a fatḥa on the lām: the plural of zulfa from the night, i.e. a portion. In al-Qāmūs: al-zulfā is a portion of the night; the plural is zulaf and zulafāt, like ghuraf and ghurafāt. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
تاج طواه الأين مما رجفا ... طيّ الليالي زلفا فزلفا
(A [camel] excellent, whom weariness has folded from his trembling, the folding of the nights, portion after portion.)
(أُتْرِفُوا): they were given luxury. Tarifa, like fariḥa, means he lived in luxury; atrafathu l-niʿma means the blessing made him insolent and made him transgress.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ): The wāw is resumptive; lā is prohibitive; تركنوا is an imperfect verb jussive by lā and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تركنوا; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila. As for فتمسكم: the fāʾ is causal; تمسكم is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied an after the fāʾ that follows a prohibition; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; and النار is the fāʿil. (وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ): The wāw is circumstantial or also resumptive, and the clause is circumstantial, i.e. "the Fire will touch you while you have no helper", or resumptive; mā is negative; لكم is a fronted khabar; من دون الله is ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أولياء; min is a redundant preposition; أولياء is genitive in form by a fatḥa, nominative in position, because it is a delayed mubtadaʾ. Thumma is a conjunction; lā is negative; تنصرون is an imperfect verb. It is not made accusative as a sequel to تركنوا, because this is a conjunction of clauses, a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal clause. (وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهارِ وَزُلَفاً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ): The wāw is a conjunction; أقم is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, implied "you"; الصلاة is mafʿūl bihi; طرفي النهار is accusative as a ẓarf attached to أقم, and what is meant by the two ends of the day is the morning and the afternoon; زلفا is also accusative as a ẓarf attached to أقم; and من الليل is naʿt. (إِنَّ الْحَسَناتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئاتِ ذلِكَ ذِكْرى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ): Inna and its noun; the clause يذهبن is its khabar; the nūn is the fāʿil of يذهبن; السيئات is mafʿūl bihi; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; ذكرى is the khabar; and للذاكرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element as naʿt of ذكرى. (وَاصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): واصبر is conjoined to أقم; the fāʾ is causal; inna and its noun; the clause لا يضيع is its khabar; and أجر المحسنين is mafʿūl bihi. (فَلَوْلا كانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ أُولُوا بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْفَسادِ فِي الْأَرْضِ): The fāʾ is resumptive; lawlā is hortative. Perhaps parsing kāna as complete is preferable, since the meaning is "why was there not found, or why did there not occur", so من القرون is attached to it or to an omitted element as ḥāl; من قبلكم is ḥāl from القرون; and أولو is its fāʿil, its sign of nominative being the wāw because it is appended to the sound masculine plural; بقية is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ينهون عن الفساد is naʿt of أولو بقية; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الفساد. If we make kāna incomplete, then من القرون is attached to an omitted element as ḥāl, the clause ينهون is its khabar, and أولو بقية is its noun. The maṣdar accompanied by the article governs overt objects, so it is more fitting for it to govern interpreted ones and ẓarfs; it may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from الفساد. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنا مِنْهُمْ): Illā is a particle of exception, and قليلا is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), lest the meaning be spoiled. We relay here the words of al-Zamakhsharī: "Its meaning is 'but a few of those We saved from the generations forbade corruption, and the rest of them abandoned forbidding'." Then he said: "If you say, 'Is there any ground on which this exception can be taken as connected?' I say: if you make it connected, as the apparent sense of the speech has it, the meaning would be corrupt, because it would then be an exhortation to those possessed of remnant to forbid corruption, and not to the few among them who were saved, as you say, 'Why did your people not recite the Qur'an, except the righteous among them?', meaning the exception of the righteous from those being exhorted to recite the Qur'an. If you say that in their being exhorted to forbid corruption lies the sense of its negation concerning them, so that it is as if it had been said 'there were not among the generations those possessed of remnant, except a few', the exception would be connected and the meaning sound, and its accusative would rest on the basic rule of exception, even though the more eloquent would be to put it in the nominative as a badal." As for ممن: it is naʿt of قليلا; the clause أنجينا is the ṣila; and منهم is ḥāl. (وَاتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ما أُتْرِفُوا فِيهِ وَكانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ): واتبع is conjoined to an implied element indicated by the speech, implied as "so they did not forbid corruption, and ... followed"; الذين is the fāʿil; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila; mā is mafʿūl bihi; the clause أترفوا is the ṣila; فيه is attached to أترفوا; كانوا مجرمين is kāna with its noun and khabar; and the clause is conjoined to أترفوا. (وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُها مُصْلِحُونَ): The wāw is resumptive; mā is negative; كان is an incomplete past verb; ربك is its noun; as for ليهلك, the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which is preceded by a negated kāna; يهلك is made accusative by an implied an after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar, i.e. "intending to destroy", and the explanation of that has already preceded; القرى is mafʿūl bihi; بظلم is ḥāl from the fāʿil; and أهلها: the wāw is circumstantial, أهلها is a mubtadaʾ and مصلحون is the khabar, and the clause is circumstantial from the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. the towns.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا», to the end of the verse, there are many arts of rhetoric before which necks are cut off, and we shall set them out as follows:

1- Harmony of expression with meaning (i'tilāf al-lafẓ maʿa l-maʿnā):
Since inclining toward those who do wrong is less than the deed of the wrongdoers, the punishment for it must be less than the punishment of the wrongdoers; and the touch of the Fire is in reality less than burning. Since burning is the punishment of the wrongdoer, justice requires that the touch be the punishment of the one who inclines to the wrongdoer. For this reason, mighty and exalted, He turned away from saying, for example, ... [Translator's note: the source has an ellipsis here and the sentence is evidently incomplete] "so that you enter the Fire", because entering is the likely occasion of burning, and He singled out the touch to point to what the inclining calls for in punishment, and to distinguish between what the wrongdoer deserves and what the one who inclines to him deserves, although the touch of the Fire may be used in a general sense meaning burning. But this general use is figurative, and the reality is what we have said, because the reality of touch is the first meeting of the body with the heat of the Fire. When an expression admits several possibilities, it is directed to what the indications point to. The harmony in this verse is in meaning.

2- Insertion (al-idmāj):
Allah the Exalted has inserted His description as just, so the art of boasting is connected with the art of discipline, since the apparent sense of the verse is discipline, and for it the admonition came in this chapter, together with the description of the True One, mighty and exalted, as just.
3- Extension (al-basṭ):
He did not say "the wrongdoers" (al-ẓālimīn) but turned to His saying «الذين ظلموا», because the first allows for the continuity of wrongdoing, which does not suit touching, and the emphasis that the second expression achieves — wrongdoing occurring only rarely — is not attained with it, so that the meaning suits the meaning of inclining and touching, and true emphasis is achieved. For when He forbids inclining toward one whose wrongdoing has continued, forbidding inclining toward one who has done wrong only once is even more fitting, and when He forbids inclining toward the wrongdoer, forbidding the deed of wrongdoing is all the more fitting.
On this occasion we record here a letter that is a sign in rhetoric and fits the occasion. When al-Zuhrī mixed with the sultans, a brother in religion wrote to him: "May Allah keep us and you, Abū Bakr, safe from trials. You have come to a state in which whoever knows you should pray to Allah for you and ask mercy for you. You have become an old man, weighed down by the favours of Allah through what He made you understand of His Book and taught you of the Sunna of His Prophet. It is not so that Allah took the covenant from the scholars; the Exalted said: «لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه». Know that the easiest of what you have committed and the lightest of what you have borne is that you have comforted the loneliness of the wrongdoer and eased the path of error by your nearness to one who did not render a right and did not abandon falsehood when he drew you near. They took you as a pivot on which the millstone of their falsehood turns, a bridge over which they cross to their trial, and a ladder by which they climb to their misguidance. Through you they introduce doubt to the scholars, and with you they lead the hearts of the ignorant. How little they built for you compared to what they ruined of yours, and how much they took from you compared to what they corrupted of your religion! What assures you that you are not among those of whom Allah said: «فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة، واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيّا»? For you deal with One who is not ignorant and who preserves against you what is not forgotten. Heal your religion, for sickness has entered it, and prepare your provisions, for the long journey has come near. «وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء». Peace."

dervis-irab:118-123.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ النَّاسَ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): The wāw is resumptive; law is a conditional particle of prevention; شاء ربك is a verb and a fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of law; جعل الناس أمة is jaʿala with its two objects; and واحدة is naʿt. (وَلا يَزالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ): The wāw is a conjunction; لا يزالون is an incomplete imperfect verb, the wāw is its noun and مختلفين is its khabar. As for إلا من رحم ربك, al-Zajjāj said it is a disconnected exception in the sense of lākin, implied as "but whoever your Lord has had mercy upon, he does not differ". Abū l-Baqāʾ was content to say: it is excepted from the fāʿil pronoun in يزالون. (وَلِذلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ): لذلك is attached to خلقهم, and the demonstrative refers to disagreement and mercy; خلقهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; تمت كلمة ربك is a verb and a fāʿil, and what is meant by His word is His eternal decree and His binding judgment. (لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ): لأملأن جهنم is the answer to an implied oath, implied as "by an oath, I shall surely fill"; أملأن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; جهنم is mafʿūl bihi; من الجنة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أملأن; al-jinna is al-jinn, and the tāʾ is for emphasis; and أجمعين is tawkīd. (وَكُلًّا نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الرُّسُلِ ما نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ): It is permissible that كلا be accusative as a maṣdar, implied as "and all the stories We relate to you", with the clause نقص عليك in the position of naʿt of his word وكلا; and it may be accusative as an object, with the muḍāf ilayhi omitted and the tanwīn as its compensation, implied as "every report We relate to you". من أنباء is naʿt of كلا; and mā is a relative noun in the accusative position as a badal from كلا, and it is also said to be redundant. On the first view it is parsed as an object, and the clause نثبت به فؤادك is the ṣila; the meaning of firming the heart is increasing its certainty and what contains the reassurance of the heart. (وَجاءَكَ فِي هذِهِ الْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): وجاءك is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi; في هذه is attached to جاءك, and the demonstrative refers to the sūra or to the reports related in it; الحق is the fāʿil of جاءك, and what follows is conjoined to it. (وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ): للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قل; the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila; اعملوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the content of the saying; and على مكانتكم is ḥāl, i.e. "while you remain firm in your standing", and the discussion of makāna has preceded. (إِنَّا عامِلُونَ): Inna and its noun and khabar. (وَانْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ): انتظروا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; إنا منتظرون is inna with its noun and khabar; and the threat is plain. (وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ الْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ): لله is a fronted khabar; غيب السموات is a delayed mubtadaʾ; إليه is attached to يرجع; الأمر is its nāʾib fāʿil; and كله is tawkīd. (فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ وَما رَبُّكَ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; اعبده is an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; وتوكل is conjoined to اعبده; عليه is attached to توكل; mā is Ḥijāzī; ربك is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; غافل is genitive in form and accusative in position, its khabar; عما is attached to غافل; and يعملون is the ṣila of mā.

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَنادى نُوحٌ رَبَّهُ فَقالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي) The wāw is resumptive. The call, as appears, was before the ship sailed, because it is a request for the rescue of his son, and there is no sense in the request except when rescue is possible. نادى نوح is a verb and an agent; ربه is a direct object; فقال: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قال is a past verb conjoined to نادى by explicative conjunction (ʿaṭf tafsīr), because the saying mentioned is the very call. رب is a muḍāf vocative added to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; inna and its noun; and من أهلي is its khabar (predicate). He brought this up only because Allah the Exalted had promised him the rescue of his family. The exegetes have a long discussion about the sonship of this son, which lies outside the scope of this book. (وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنْتَ أَحْكَمُ الْحاكِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; inna, its noun and its khabar; وأنت أحكم الحاكمين is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is also conjoined. (قالَ يا نُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ) قال is a past verb whose agent is the latent pronoun of Allah; inna and its noun, and the clause ليس من أهلك is the khabar of إن, and من أهلك is the khabar of ليس. (إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ) inna and its noun; the pronoun refers to his son, and there is no justification for the statement of those who said that the pronoun refers to his request, as al-Jalāl and others held, because the eloquence of the speech rules it out. عمل is the khabar of إن, and this is a case of putting the adjective in the place of the thing described when the meaning is apparent, which has already been pointed out. Of it is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
أيها القائل في غير الصواب ... أخّر النصح وأقلل من عتابي
(O you who speak other than what is right, put off your counsel and lessen your reproach of me.)
and his saying also:
وكم من قتيل لا يباء به دم ... ومن غلق رهنا إذا ضمّه منى ومن مالىء عينيه من شيء غيره ... إذا راح نحو الجمرة البيض كالدمى
(How many a slain man for whom no blood is paid in retribution, and how many a pledge left pawned when Minā gathers him, and one who fills his eyes with nothing but her, when the white ones like statues head toward the Jamra.)
[Translator's note: the two verses seem to be run together in the source, and the text is as printed; my gloss is tentative.]
He meant "O man, the killer" and "how many a man slain". And the saying of al-Khansāʾ:
ترتع ما رتعت حتى إذا ادّكرت ... فإنما هي إقبال وإدبار
(She grazes as long as she grazes, until, when she remembers, she is nothing but approaching and turning away.)
غير صالح is an adjective of عمل, and the clause is a reason for the negation of his being among his family who are saved. (فَلا تَسْئَلْنِ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ) The fāʾ is the eloquent (faṣīḥa) fāʾ; لا is prohibitive; تسأل is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, is a direct object; ما is a second direct object; the clause ليس is a ṣila; the noun of ليس is علم and لك is its fronted khabar; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to علم. (إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ) inna and its noun, and the clause أعظك is its khabar; أن and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "I warn you against being", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أعظك; the noun of تكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and من الجاهلين is the khabar of تكون. The meaning of calling Nūḥ's request ignorance will come in the Benefits section. (قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْئَلَكَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ) inna and its noun, and the clause أعوذ is its khabar; بك is attached to أعوذ; أن and what is in its domain are accusative by removal of the preposition; and the i'rab of ما ليس لي به علم has already been given. (وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي أَكُنْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional and لا is negative; تغفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; وترحمني is conjoined to تغفر; أكن is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; and من الخاسرين is its khabar. (قِيلَ يا نُوحُ اهْبِطْ بِسَلامٍ مِنَّا وَبَرَكاتٍ عَلَيْكَ) اهبط is an imperative verb; بسلام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of اهبط, i.e. "accompanied by peace"; منا is an adjective of سلام, or is attached to سلام itself; وبركات is conjoined to سلام; and عليك is an adjective. (وَعَلى أُمَمٍ مِمَّنْ مَعَكَ) وعلى أمم is conjoined to عليك; ممن is an adjective of أمم; and معك is an adverbial of place, the ṣila of the relative. (وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُمْ مِنَّا عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; أمم is a mubtadaʾ, and it was permissible to begin with it because it is qualified, the implied form being "and nations from among those with you"; and the clause سنمتعهم is its khabar; or سنمتعهم is made an adjective and the omitted part is the khabar, omitted because his saying ممن معك indicates it. ثم is a conjunction implying delay; يمسهم is an imperfect verb and a direct object; منا is a ḥāl because it was an adjective of عذاب; عذاب is the agent; and أليم is a second adjective. (تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيها إِلَيْكَ) تلك is a mubtadaʾ; من أنباء الغيب is a first khabar; and the clause نوحيها إليك is a second khabar, and if you wish it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "that being of the tidings of the unseen, revealed to you". (ما كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُها أَنْتَ وَلا قَوْمُكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا) It is a third khabar, and this is the best of the i'rabs; كان and its noun, and the clause تعلمها is the khabar of كنت, and ها is a direct object; أنت is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent agent of تعلمها; ولا قومك is conjoined to أنت; and من قبل هذا is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in نوحيها or of the kāf in إليك, i.e. "you and your people being ignorant of it". (فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ الْعاقِبَةَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if you have learned this story and what it contains and what the event of the Flood came to, then be patient"; and the clause إن العاقبة للمتقين, inna with its noun and khabar, gives a reason. This is the purpose of the story of Nūḥ and the stories that will follow it.

* Benefits:
The exegetes have a long discussion on this verse and on the reason for describing Nūḥ's request as ignorance, which indicates a lack of infallibility (ʿiṣma); al-Zamakhsharī even held that there issued from Nūḥ, peace be upon him, what makes it necessary to ascribe ignorance to him and to reproach him for it. It would be long to quote what they adduced, or even to summarize it. The closest thing that can be said about it is that when the promise was issued to Nūḥ of the rescue of his family, except those of them against whom the word had already gone forth, he was not one who had uncovered the condition of his said son, nor was he informed of his inner self and the reality of his affair; rather he believed, from the outward condition, that he was a believer. So he stayed with holding to the general wording on account of established family membership, and no certainty of his son's disbelief opposed it so as to take him out of the family and put him among the excepted. So he asked Allah about him on that basis, and it became clear to him that in His knowledge he was among the excepted, and that he himself had no knowledge of that; therefore he asked about him.
